candidates.full: Для компаний, которые разрабатывают на заказ: один стек на всех клиентов, ИИ‑помощник, который пишет компилирующийся маршрут, схема процесса для аналитика клиента и лицензия без строки в смете. Кудаж без ИИ, теперь это реальный инструмент и с хорошей головой применив можно получить отличный результат. Сколько часов в вашем последнем проекте ушло на то, за что клиент не хочет платить отдельной строкой? Подключение к брокеру, повторы и защита от дублей, миграции базы, выкладка, мониторинг. В смете это прячут в «архитектуру» и «интеграцию», а клиент всё равно спрашивает, почему так долго. Я двадцать с лишним лет делаю бэкенды на заказ, и последние три с лишним года делаю их на собственной открытой экосистеме redb для.NET. Ниже о том, почему для компании, которая разрабатывает на заказ, это удобный стек: что ускоряется, что легче сдавать клиенту и где у него честные границы. Одни и те же кирпичи у каждого клиента Экосистема состоит из хранилища данных, интеграционного движка redb.Route, хоста для модулей redb.Tsak и сервера входа redb.Identity. Данные — это класс C#, процесс — это маршрут, внешняя система — строка адреса. У каждого клиента одна и та же структура проекта. Проект начинается с шаблона. Для маршрутов их 21: файлы, Kafka, RabbitMQ, почта, REST, AS2, AS4, хранилище redb и другие. Есть шаблоны приложений и воркера. По моему опыту, второй проект на этом стеке идёт заметно быстрее первого, а третий быстрее второго: решения не изобретаются заново, а новый человек в команде видит знакомую структуру с первого дня. ИИ‑помощник, который пишет маршрут, а не догадки Для компании, которая продаёт часы, это, пожалуй, главное. В каждый проект из шаблона уже положен файл AGENTS.md с правилами для GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Codex и Claude Code: какие элементы брать, как хранить секреты, что проверять. Маршрут описывается типизированным DSL, а XML‑схема генерируется из настоящих пакетов, поэтому помощник работает с тем, что реально существует. Если он всё‑таки выдумает опцию, проверка пакета откажет до выкладки, назовёт файл, строку и колонку и подскажет правильное имя. Ошибку ловит проверка у разработчика, а не сервер клиента. Помощник ускоряет разработчика, но не заменяет его: свой код с бизнес‑расчётом по‑прежнему пишется на C#, и отвечает за него человек. Красивый код, если держаться DSL Вот маршрут: читать заказы из Kafka, пропускать только новые и отправлять в RabbitMQ. From("kafka://orders?groupId=svc&brokers=localhost:9092") .Filter(Header("type").isEqualTo("new")) .To("rabbitmq://events?host=localhost"); То же самое в XML: <route id="orders"> <from uri="kafka://orders?groupId=svc&brokers=localhost:9092"/> <filter expr="header.type == 'new'"> <to uri="rabbitmq://events?host=localhost"/> </filter> </route> Повторы, обработка ошибок, транзакции и мёртвые письма описываются в том же стиле. Код разных разработчиков и разных проектов выглядит одинаково, и ревью не тратится на спор о том, как правильно. Вот так выглядит настоящий маршрут из демо‑проекта: проверка по схеме, обработка ошибки, решение и ответ в одной транзакции, с комментариями, которые читаются как описание процесса. Сдача проекта: схема, которую читает аналитик клиента Обычно после сдачи клиент остаётся с кодом, который понимает один человек, и этот человек ваш. Здесь процесс описан маршрутом, а маршрут можно показать картинкой. Утилита redb-route-xml рисует по XML‑маршруту блок‑схему в формате Mermaid: redb-route-xml mermaid routes/main.route.xml --bin bin/Debug/net10.0 Mermaid показывают GitHub, GitLab и многие просмотрщики Markdown. Аналитик клиента смотрит на схему и проверяет, что процесс устроен так, как договаривались, без разработчика рядом. В VS Code есть бесплатное расширение, которое показывает тот же маршрут графом прямо поверх XML, а команда redb Route: Show Mermaid Diagram открывает схему Mermaid в соседней вкладке, без терминала: Клиент меньше зависит от конкретного человека, а вы меньше времени тратите на объяснения. Лицензия без строки в смете Ядро, интеграционный движок, хост и сервер входа открыты под Apache 2.0. Pro‑пакеты закрыты, но бесплатны. Чтобы не пересказывать, вот что написано в самой лицензии Pro: install, configure, and run the Software, for any lawful purpose, including in commercial and production environments (§ 2.1 a) no limit on the number of developers, servers, or requests (§ 2.1 b) Allow the Licensee's employees, contractors, and agents to use the Software on the Licensee's behalf (§ 2.1 d) The Software is provided free of charge. No purchase, payment, license key, activation, subscription, or renewal is required (§ 2.2) Distributing an application that merely uses the Software as a dependency is permitted (§ 3.1 a) Для консалтинга это значит: вы строите на redb решение для клиента, клиент запускает его у себя, и ни вам, ни ему ничего не нужно покупать и активировать. Нельзя другое: распространять или продавать сами Pro‑пакеты как отдельный продукт или библиотеку и делать на их основе конкурирующий продукт (§ 3.1). Всё в контуре клиента Ничего не нужно заказывать у поставщика: нет SaaS, нет сервера лицензий, система ничего не отправляет наружу. Данные лежат в базе клиента: PostgreSQL, SQL Server или SQLite. Служба безопасности клиента проверяет то, что видит: пакеты NuGet, образы контейнеров, подписанные cosign, и открытый исходный код. Закрытые Pro‑пакеты тоже не чёрный ящик: их исходники мы по запросу передаём компаниям для проверки безопасности. Для банков и госзаказчиков это часто снимает вопрос ещё до пилота. На больших объёмах это тоже работает: например, в одном проекте больше 1 млн объектов и больше 47 млн значений свойств. Выкладка: модуль, а не релиз всей системы Маршруты клиента живут модулями в хосте redb.Tsak. Что получает команда DevOps у клиента или у вас: - Три способа поставки хоста на выбор. Готовые Docker‑образы (redb-tsak-worker, redb-tsak-web, redb-tsak-stack), самодостаточные архивы для Linux и Windows без установленного.NET или свой хост, собранный из NuGet в вашем конвейере: dotnet new tsak-worker из redb.Tsak.Templates даёт Worker Service на services.AddTsak(configuration) с Dockerfile. - Проверяемые артефакты. Образы и архивы подписаны cosign, конвейер клиента проверяет их cosign verify до выкладки. - Хранилище под задачу. По умолчанию SQLite: один сервер, ставить ничего не нужно. Для кластера PostgreSQL или SQL Server. - Модуль одним файлом. Пакет .tpkg кладут в папку modules/ или выкладывают tsak module deploy. Хост запускает новую версию, старая дорабатывает начатые сообщения и останавливается, остальные модули узла выкладку не замечают. Откат — tsak module rollback. - Подсказка для конвейера. Перед выкладкой CI спрашивает узел (tsak system deploy-advice), можно ли менять модуль на горячую или нужен холодный путь, и получает ответ кодом выхода, который понимает любой CI. - Kubernetes. Готовые манифесты, пробы startup, live и ready, вывод узла из работы (cordon) и возврат. - Наблюдаемость. Эндпоинт Prometheus, трассы OpenTelemetry, готовый дашборд Grafana и локальный стенд Prometheus + Grafana + Jaeger в docker compose. - Режимы API. Полный, без портов для встраивания или только чтение для мониторинга. Рядом CLI tsak и клиентский пакет для своих инструментов (services.AddTsakClient). Для консалтинга это значит, что правка для клиента — это один модуль, а не релиз всей системы с ночным окном. Клиент видит, что происходит, сам, без вашего разработчика: дашборд показывает каждый маршрут с его трафиком, ошибками и состоянием. Там же мониторинг узла: процессор, память, потоки и сборка мусора, а рядом список модулей, планировщик, журнал, аудит и недоставленные сообщения. Подписанные модули: вы собираете, клиент разворачивает Модуль можно подписать. Вы один раз создаёте пару ключей (tsak module keygen), подписываете каждый пакет модуля в своём CI (tsak module sign) и отдаёте клиенту публичный ключ. Узел клиента с этим ключом примет только подписанный вами модуль: неподписанный или подменённый пакет он отвергнет. Клиент разворачивает обновления сам, в своём Tsak, а вы точно знаете, что у него работает именно ваша сборка. Готовые позиции для коммерческого предложения Часть того, что обычно приходится обещать «сделаем», уже есть: - Документооборот с Европой. Коннектор AS4: версия 4.6.1 прошла тестирование соответствия Еврокомиссии, 76 из 76 обязательных тестов, и redb.Route.As4 внесён в список продуктов, соответствующих eDelivery AS4 (общий профиль). Для клиента, которому партнёр в ЕС прописал AS4 в договоре, это готовый ответ, а не отдельный Java‑шлюз в смете. Подробности в статье про AS4. Рядом AS2 для партнёров, которые работают по нему. - Интеграции. 30 транспортных пакетов: Kafka, RabbitMQ, IBM MQ, SQL, HTTP, SOAP, SFTP, почта, облачные очереди и другие. - Эксплуатация. Дашборд хоста: маршруты, ошибки, недоставленные сообщения, журнал, метрики, кластер. Несколько клиентов на одной экосистеме — это отдельная база на каждого. Специального «режима многоарендности» нет, изоляция идёт по базам, и так проще объяснить её службе безопасности. Честные границы - Частые релизы. Отдельной ветки долгой поддержки нет. Текущая линия 4.7.x получает исправления критичных ошибок и исправления по запросу; с 4.8.0 пакеты собираются только под.NET 10 и 11. Закладывайте обновления в сопровождение. - Хост кто‑то держит. Сервер, ОС, TLS и бэкапы базы — работа администратора клиента или ваша, если вы её продаёте. - Свой код остаётся вашим. Бизнес‑расчёт и коннектор, которого нет в списке, пишутся на C#. Что я предлагаю Не переводить всех клиентов разом. Возьмите одного клиента и одну интеграцию, которая у вас сейчас болит, соберите её на redb и сравните часы с тем, как вы делаете это обычно. Код и документация: github.com/redbase‑app, статьи: redb.ru/articles. А какая часть ваших проектов повторяется от клиента к клиенту, и сколько часов она съедает? Расскажите в комментариях. Він пішов би на такий крок лише за умови, що був би переконаний: це однозначно відповідає національним інтересам Америки, а ширші безпекові домовленості роблять застосування цієї гарантії вкрай малоймовірним. Саме тому гарантії безпеки для України не можуть бути остаточно узгоджені у відриві від повоєнної архітектури європейської безпеки. Ці два питання необхідно розглядати разом», — зазначив він. 13 листопада під час спілкування з представниками ЗМІ президент Володимир Зеленський розповів, що влада США пропонує Україні гарантії, «схожі на статті 4 і 5» Статуту НАТО. Однак, за словами глави Української держави, на його запитання про те, чи перебуватимуть у такому разі на українській землі американські військові, у Вашингтоні відповіли відмовою. 18 листопада агентство Bloomberg повідомило, що американські представники чинять тиск на російських та українських посадовців, аби ті розглянули нові пропозиції щодо НАТО, військових ресурсів і розміщення військ у Європі в межах переговорів про припинення війни.

candidates.title: Brake Check: Hijacking Trailer Brakes over Bluetooth
candidates.summary: Nine Things a Microsoft 365 Security Review Finds Almost Every Time The same findings come up in nearly every tenant we assess. Nine of them, what each one actually costs you, and how to check your own as you read. All resources Brake Check: Hijacking Trailer Brakes Over Bluetooth Any phone in Blue
candidates.full: Nine Things a Microsoft 365 Security Review Finds Almost Every Time The same findings come up in nearly every tenant we assess. Nine of them, what each one actually costs you, and how to check your own as you read. All resources Brake Check: Hijacking Trailer Brakes Over Bluetooth Any phone in Bluetooth range could apply an Elecbrakes trailer brake controller at any force, with no pairing. How we found it, the fix, and the six-month disclosure. By Patrick Forck and Jeremy McCarthy, Element Digital Disclosure status: This vulnerability was reported to Elecbrakes under coordinated disclosure on 18 May 2026. Elecbrakes shipped a firmware fix for the EB2 and VM1 on 6 July 2026, seven weeks later. If you own one, open the app and install the firmware update before reading on. The update doesn’t install itself: you have to open the app and start it. You want EB2 firmware 3.0.4.4.3 or later, or VM1 firmware 1.3.4.2.1 or later. Go on, we’ll wait. If you own the older ELBC 2000, there is no fix yet. Elecbrakes has confirmed it has the same vulnerability, so every Elecbrakes controller - both models on sale today and the one before them - was affected. See the ELBC 2000 section below. This write-up follows the disclosure date agreed with Elecbrakes (15 November 2026), four months after the fix reached the field. Elecbrakes tells us it is not aware of any reported incidents of damage or injury caused by these vulnerabilities. CISA’s advisory, published on 19 November, covers three CVEs - CVE-2026-96805 (CVSS 9.6, Critical), CVE-2026-125273 and CVE-2026-124281. The coordination process took considerably longer than the research did, which is itself covered further down. Any phone or laptop within Bluetooth range of an Elecbrakes trailer brake controller could apply that trailer’s brakes - at any force, at highway speed - without pairing, a PIN, or any authentication whatsoever. Four bytes. No handshake. No “are you sure?” The longer version has drive tests, a fuzzing session that lit up like a Christmas tree, an over-the-air (OTA) firmware channel with the security posture of a screen door, a small Australian manufacturer that engineered a genuinely good fix at impressive speed, and a coordination process afterwards that turned out to be harder and slower than any of the technical work. Let’s get into it. This research didn’t begin with a threat model or a scope document. It began with me driving down the highway and noticing that my Elecbrakes In-Car Remote had connected to someone else’s trailer. I didn’t have my trailer on my car but I did have the remote powered on in the centre console. It had connected mid-drive, without pairing or a prompt, to a brake controller that wasn’t mine, on a trailer I’d never seen, belonging to a driver who had no idea. The trailers this happened with most often are operated by Sensys Gatso for the Tasmanian Government, and look very similar to this: Photo: Richard J. Ho, Minch Media For the non-Tasmanians that may not recognise the trailer If you do security work, you know the feeling. That little cold prickle at the back of your neck that says hang on, that shouldn’t be possible - and it would be very bad if it were. If a device I don’t own will happily talk to my in-car remote driving past with zero friction… what exactly is stopping my phone or any other Bluetooth device from talking back? Turns out: nothing. It was very happy to accept our ‘requests’. I own the trailer. I own the in-car remote. I have a professional interest in devices that will do dangerous things for anyone who asks, with no friction in the way. So my colleague Jeremy and I decided to find out how deep it went. (For the record, and for the lawyers: every single test in this post was performed on our own hardware, on private property or a closed setup. We never touched another person’s vehicle. The “connecting to strangers” bit was the in-car remote doing that by itself, which is rather the point.) If you don’t tow things, here’s the deal. Trailers over a certain weight need their own brakes, and those brakes need a controller that applies them in proportion to how hard the tow vehicle is braking. Historically this was a box bolted under your dashboard. Elecbrakes’ clever idea was to move that box onto the trailer itself and control it over Bluetooth from an app or a little remote. Mount it once, tow with any vehicle, no re-wiring. It’s a nice bit of kit, which is partly why it’s so popular on Australian caravans, boat trailers, and horse floats. Elecbrakes currently sells two models - the EB2 (the device I own) and the VM1. We have confirmed with Elecbrakes that these operate the same Bluetooth stack, so both were susceptible to this vulnerability. There’s also an older model, the ELBC 2000, which hasn’t been sold for a number of years but is still out there on trailers. Elecbrakes has since confirmed it has the same vulnerability, and it has no fix yet. More on that further down. The important word here is proportional. This device decides how much braking force your trailer applies. It is, unambiguously, a safety-critical component. When it does the right thing, towing is smoother and safer. When it does the wrong thing, you are having a very bad day on a highway with several tonnes of trailer behind you. Keep that framing in mind, because everything below is a story about a safety-critical device that trusted anyone who said hello. Here’s the honest bit that’s relevant to the whole story. Jeremy and I work in infrastructure, cloud and security. Between us we’ve spent a couple of decades deciding what “good” looks like and developing a nose for what “bad” smells like. What we are not is Android developers, and neither of us can sit down and read 5,000 lines of decompiled Smali bytecode. So we didn’t. We used AI - Claude in this case - to do the heavy lifting on the reverse engineering. We pulled the Elecbrakes Android app (com.ElecBrake.Remote), decompiled it, and fed it to Claude with a simple set of questions: What Bluetooth characteristics does this thing talk to? What’s the command format? Where’s the authentication? The app itself is a perfectly respectable modern Android build - Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, a Nordic-style Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) stack. What came back from the analysis was a map of the device’s entire Bluetooth GATT profile: 47 characteristics across four services, commands sent as plain unencrypted byte arrays, no checksums, no sequence numbers. And that last question - where’s the authentication? - came back with the most ominous possible answer for a brake controller: it couldn’t find any on the control path. Not weak auth. Not broken auth. No auth code at all on the characteristic that mattered. We also noticed the app only shows itself 42 of the 47 characteristics. It carries a UUID allow-list and quietly ignores the other five. Hiding characteristics from your own app’s UI is a “note to self” at best. But it did tell us there was more surface here than the official app admitted to. Naturally, we wanted to see all of it. There’s a broader point here worth sitting with. This kind of research used to require a fairly rare and specific skill set. It now requires curiosity, a device you own, and an AI that can read bytecode faster than any human. The barrier to finding this class of bug just dropped through the floor, which is a lesson for every vendor shipping a connected product. To talk to the whole device, including the parts the official app hid, we needed our own tool. Jeremy built one with Claude on the first night swarm mode was available in Australia, in between Forza races. What it produced from a single prompt was a Web Bluetooth research tool that runs in Chrome and an Android app for the same purpose. While the Android app was built, we didn’t end up using it as the Chrome tool had more than enough capabilities for what we needed. This required no specialised hardware, no BLE sniffer, no software-defined radio. A browser tab on my Windows 11 laptop. The single most alarming fact in this entire write-up is that the complete attacker toolkit is a device with Chrome and Bluetooth - the same laptop you’d use to check your email, order a pizza, or, in our case, lose repeatedly at Forza. The best part of building it this way was the iteration speed. Every time the device did something surprising, we’d describe the new capability we wanted - an opcode fuzzer, a persistent-register reader, a state-change listener - and have it a few minutes later. The tooling kept pace with our curiosity. If the device did something odd at 10am, we had a tool to probe it before 11. We were essentially building the instrument and running the experiment in the same breath. With my newly built tool on my laptop I headed down to our family shack for the day, which has a few acres of land and some private gravel roads to test on, and where my trailer lives most of its life. I tethered my phone, launched our app and got testing. Everything that follows was found in the next four hours. This wasn’t a multi-day attack. The test setup: my laptop, phone and trailer. Using Web Bluetooth’s optionalServices to bypass the app’s UUID allow-list, we connected and dumped the full unfiltered GATT profile. And there it was, in black and white: Service: b49c1e5f-... (EB2 primary service) R W N User Commands 18315e96-... <-- BRAKE CONTROL R W N State/Warnings 2f4d4806-... <-- BRAKE STATE R W N Program 1-5, System Params, Comms... Service: 2f413b1e-... (OTA / pairing-gated service) R N Central Command 799b1b62-... <-- PAIRING REQUIRED R W N Central Response c0244a8a-... <-- PAIRING REQUIRED The device has two tiers. Some things require Bluetooth pairing. Some things don’t. Guess which tier brake control was in. We tried to subscribe to everything, without pairing. The device’s response is almost poetic in how precisely it protects the wrong things. (Timestamps in these logs are UTC, so 23:40 was 9:40am local time.) [23:40:24.739] Failed to subscribe Bonding: GATT Error: Not paired. [23:40:25.217] Subscribed: User Commands <-- brake control, NO PAIRING [23:40:25.877] Subscribed: State/Warnings <-- brake state, NO PAIRING [23:40:26.702] Failed to subscribe Central Command: GATT Error: Not paired. [23:40:26.972] Failed to subscribe Central Response: GATT Error: Not paired. Look at that. The device is perfectly capable of saying “Not paired.” It says it four times! It checks ID at the door for the bonding characteristic. It checks ID for the firmware update channel. And then, for brake control - the one function that can put a caravan through a guardrail - it waves you straight through without so much as a glance. The bouncer is meticulous about everything except the thing worth guarding. So we wrote four bytes to the brake control characteristic. No pairing, no PIN, no prior anything: [23:40:39.841] WRITE User Commands: 14 00 00 00 [23:40:39.977] WRITE User Commands: OK [23:40:40.008] NOTIFY State/Warnings: 03 00 00 20 ... ^^ 0x03 = brakes ENERGISED The electromagnetic hum at the brake drums was immediate and, frankly, a little sickening. That OK is the sound of a safety-critical device with no survival instinct - it said yes to four bytes from a total stranger then energised several tonnes’ worth of brakes and reported back that it had done so, pleased with itself. Release is exactly as easy: [23:53:00.312] WRITE User Commands: 00 00 00 00 [23:53:00.472] NOTIFY State/Warnings: 00 00 00 20 ... ^^ 0x00 = brakes RELEASED And here’s the thing that turns this from “spooky demo” into “genuine attacker capability”: the State/Warnings characteristic notifies you back on every state change. 0x00 → 0x03 when the brakes engage, 0x03 → 0x00 when they release. The device gives an attacker a real-time read receipt confirming their command worked. You don’t even have to guess. The command format decodes as: 14 00 00 00 ^opcode ^force ^ignored 0x14 0x00-0xFF Byte 0 is the opcode. Byte 1 scales electromagnetic force from a gentle nudge to maximum. Which brings us to the drive test. You could reasonably ask whether that force byte does anything meaningful, or whether “maximum” is a rounding error. So we took it to a road (ours, closed, researcher-owned, etc.) and found out. [00:56:31.248] WRITE User Commands: 14 00 00 00 <-- minimum force [00:56:46.171] WRITE User Commands: 14 FF 00 00 <-- maximum force 14 FF 00 00 produced dramatically stronger deceleration than 14 00 00 00 at the same speed. The force byte is a linear scale from “polite tap” to “slamming the brakes”, and any Bluetooth device in range gets the full dial. Sit with the highway version of that for a second. Your trailer’s brakes slamming to maximum while your tow vehicle keeps going is the exact recipe for a jackknife - one of the more reliably fatal things a vehicle combination can do. And the attacker needs to know precisely nothing about you. At this point an optimist might hope that 0x14 is a magic number - that an attacker would at least need to know the right opcode. So we fuzzed the whole first byte, 0x00 through 0xFF, and listened. It lit up everywhere. 0x01-0x13 Low power (very quiet - ear-to-the-wheel quiet) 0x14 Standard (the "official" opcode) 0x15-0x19 Standard (adjacent cluster) 0x4A-0x4B ABS / pulse (higher pitch) 0x4C-0x51 Standard 0x52-0x64+ ABS / pulse We haven’t confirmed the ABS, standard and low-power modes with Elecbrakes. They’re our assumptions, based on the real-world effects and the sound of the electromagnets while we tested. Practically every non-zero value for that first byte activates the brakes at some force, in some mode. There is no secret handshake to reverse. An attacker doesn’t need our research, doesn’t need the app, doesn’t need the protocol docs. They can write approximately any garbage to that characteristic and the trailer will brake. We found ABS-style pulse modes by accident, just by sweeping the range and noticing the pitch change. When the naive attack and the sophisticated attack are the same attack, you don’t have an authentication weakness. You have an authentication absence. A few other findings rounded out the picture: - No replay protection. Raw GATT writes, no nonces, no timestamps, no session tokens. Capture a legitimate command once, replay it forever. - A persistent command register. The control characteristic remembers the last value written to it, across reconnects, with no timeout. Reconnect later, read it back, and you can see the last command the device received - a quiet little intelligence leak. - Connection-dependent release. The one accidental mercy: when the attacker’s Bluetooth connection drops, the brakes release after 2–5 seconds. This limits a pure drive-by, but does nothing to stop a stationary attacker who simply stays in range - think a boat trailer on a ramp, or a caravan parked on a hill. Everything so far is transient - hold the connection, hold the brakes; drop it, they let go. The firmware update channel is where it stops being transient. The OTA service is behind pairing, which sounds reassuring right up until you learn what kind of pairing. We paired using Windows’ bog-standard “Add a device” dialog. It used Just Works mode - no PIN, no passkey, no numeric comparison, no user friction of any kind. Just Works is the Bluetooth pairing mode that provides encryption against a passive eavesdropper and essentially nothing against an active attacker who’s actually trying. Once paired, the OTA channel accepted arbitrary writes to its 255-byte buffer without complaint: [03:04:26.639] WRITE Central Response: 14 FF 00 00 [03:04:26.768] WRITE Central Response: OK We stopped there deliberately - we did not attempt to flash modified firmware to a live device, because I didn’t want to brick a brake controller worth about $800 that I own and we had already found plenty of issues that day. But we did the static analysis back in the office on the firmware image the app itself distributes, and that told us plenty. The image is “encrypted,” but the decryption key ships inside every copy of the app. It’s a lock with the key taped to the front, mailed to everyone who downloads the app from the Play Store or the App Store. Once decrypted, the integrity story is the real problem: the entire update pipeline is protected by CRC32 checksums and nothing else. We confirmed this three independent ways - the firmware descriptor carries only CRCs, the device-side DFU protocol transmits only CRCs, and the decrypted image itself contains zero cryptographic signature material (no signature block, no verification strings, nothing). The “start firmware update” handshake is a fixed 16-byte constant that’s identical for every image, so it works as a static unlock token. A CRC protects against a cosmic ray flipping a bit in transit. It does absolutely nothing against an attacker, because anyone modifying the firmware just recalculates the CRC. There’s a boundary worth calling out - the final “accept or reject” decision lives in the bootloader, which sits in a separate flash region we couldn’t pull without physically wiring up the chip. So this is “no signature material exists anywhere we can see in software,” not “we flashed evil firmware and it booted.” But every layer we could inspect points the same direction, and it’s the direction that lets a paired attacker theoretically write persistent firmware that disables braking on a speed or GPS trigger, decouples the brake lights from the actual brakes, or quietly logs where a vehicle goes. These devices do have a GPS module and gyroscope sensor, so there are a lot of possibilities if you can get into the firmware. That’s the difference between “hold the connection to hold the brakes” and “the brakes are compromised after you’ve driven away.” Most of the connected-device bugs we all read about are about data - a leaked database, a hijacked camera, a smart lock that opens. Bad, but bounded. This one outputs torque to a wheel on a public road. The impact isn’t measured in records exposed. It’s measured in stopping distances, jackknife angles, and boat ramps. A loaded boat trailer is commonly 1.5 to 4 tonnes; a caravan on a mountain descent is relying on those trailer brakes to stay within the tow vehicle’s capacity. The attack surface is “anyone within Bluetooth range,” the skill required is “can write four bytes,” and the victim selection is “optional.” To keep the risk in proportion: Elecbrakes tells us there have been no reported incidents of damage or injury caused by these vulnerabilities, and we haven’t seen evidence of exploitation either. A brake application that ends when the connection drops leaves little behind, so that’s reassuring rather than conclusive, and it’s one more reason to install the update. There’s a regulatory dimension too, which we flagged to Elecbrakes in the disclosure. I am going to also preface this with, I am clearly not a lawyer, and my understanding of Australian law is crude at best. In Australia, trailer braking is governed by ADR 38/05, which requires the brake control to be progressively increased and decreased by means of the ‘Control Signal’ from the towing vehicle. A stranger applying your brakes from the footpath is rather obviously contrary to that. Layer on the Australian Consumer Law’s safety obligations and you have a situation where a Bluetooth bug and a compliance problem are the same problem. We didn’t raise that to be threatening; we raised it because a vendor deciding how urgently to act deserves the full picture. Partway through the coordination, I came across an older Elecbrakes controller by chance, on a trailer in my local area: an ELBC 2000. candidates.title: In Other News: Norwegian Energy Firm Cyberattacks, Supercomputer Hack, New Nightmare Eclipse Exploit
candidates.summary: SecurityWeek’s weekly cybersecurity news roundup offers a concise overview of important developments that may not receive full standalone coverage yet remain relevant to the broader threat landscape. This curated summary highlights key stories across vulnerability disclosures, emerging attack method
candidates.full: SecurityWeek’s weekly cybersecurity news roundup offers a concise overview of important developments that may not receive full standalone coverage yet remain relevant to the broader threat landscape. This curated summary highlights key stories across vulnerability disclosures, emerging attack methods, policy updates, industry reports, and other noteworthy events to help readers stay well-informed about the evolving cybersecurity environment. Here are this week’s highlights: Gemini agents targeted Epoch AI AI evaluation firm Trajectory Labs says Gemini 4 Argon agents it stress-tested in October, with Gemini’s API safeguards turned on, tried to hack Epoch AI’s live website while hunting for answers to non-existent FrontierMath problems, attempting SQL injection and impersonating Epoch staff. Trajectory has paused all misalignment testing. Epoch says no private information was accessed. Google brings Gemini 4 Neon to defenders Google has released Gemini 4 Neon, a faster, lower-cost model for coding and enterprise work, and says a cyber-focused version will reach eligible members of its Fairwind Program for trusted defenders in the coming days. Google claims the model performs at frontier level across finding, validating and patching vulnerabilities. It also says Neon keeps Carbon-level safeguards against cyber and biosecurity misuse while turning down far fewer legitimate requests in those areas. Compromised migration vendor opens door to Infoblox data theft Networking and security company Infoblox has confirmed that hackers accessed certain company information through a compromised third-party data migration vendor, which TechCrunch’s sources say handled SharePoint migration. The Register has since reported that the stolen files included NIOS configuration snapshots for some customers and personal details of employees and their dependents. Infoblox says it has no indication that its products, cloud services, software updates or build-and-release processes were involved. EU adds NoName057(16) to cyber sanctions list The Council of the EU has sanctioned 30 individuals and two entities over Russian information manipulation and cyber activity, including the Moscow-based Social Design Agency, 24 of its employees, and several pro-Kremlin propagandists. Under its cyber sanctions regime, the Council also listed NoName057(16), the pro-Russian group that has claimed attacks on government bodies, critical infrastructure and companies in Ukraine, the US and EU member states. Japanese supercomputer offline after intrusion Japan’s Riken research institute has suspended operations of the Fugaku supercomputer and cut off external access after detecting suspicious traffic on its user authentication system. In a November 17 notice, Riken said an outside party used a public dashboard showing Fugaku’s operational status to break into the system’s internal operations network and tamper with multiple servers. Names, email addresses and user IDs of up to 4,597 Fugaku and RIKYU users may have been exposed. Ukraine arrests ransomware suspects, 8-Digits member extradited to US Ukrainian police, working with the FBI, have arrested four alleged key members of a ransomware gang that posed as IT support in calls powered by an AI voice platform to obtain credentials or get remote access software installed. Separately, Kazakh national Roman Khlynovskiy has appeared in US court after being extradited from Italy over his alleged role in the 8-Digits Team, an INC and Lynx ransomware affiliate accused of stealing data from US hospitals, healthcare entities and schools and making over $500 million in ransom demands. In Florida, five people were arrested in a nationwide crackdown on account-takeover fraud schemes linked to more than $54 million in losses at over 65 US financial institutions. Test environment intrusion exposes Rakuten Securities customer data Japanese online brokerage Rakuten Securities says login IDs and branch codes for up to 11.25 million accounts, and personal and financial information for up to 4.47 million accounts, may have been exposed after attackers accessed a test environment system on November 11. The exposed details include names, dates of birth, addresses, employers, withdrawal bank account numbers, and declared annual income and financial assets. Equinor stops cyberattack as Skagerak Energi reports attempted intrusion Norwegian energy giant Equinor says it has stopped a cyberattack against some of its IT systems that it detected on November 17, adding that production was not affected and there is no sign that data was stolen or altered. The company said the attack was not a virus attack and did not appear to be specifically targeting it. A day after Equinor’s disclosure, Norwegian power company Skagerak Energi reported activity that may have been an attempted cyberattack on some of its IT systems, saying operations and production were not affected and there is no sign that information was leaked. Nightmare Eclipse drops unpatched Windows lock screen escape Researcher Nightmare Eclipse has published FastUnlock, an unpatched Windows 11 zero-day that abuses the Narrator screen reader to get past the lock screen and run code as the lock screen account. The attack requires physical access and at least one account linked to an online Microsoft account. Malware targets CACs left in personal computers The NSA says threat actors are using malware against the personal computers that Department of War (DoW) employees use with Common Access Card (CAC) readers. Once the malware has recorded the card’s PIN, it can use the CAC’s credentials to sign into federal and DoW websites for as long as the card stays in the reader. That often gives attackers access to anything the cardholder can normally reach. Related: In Other News: New CISA Director Nominee, Connected Car Hacking, Baker Tilly Data Breach Related: In Other News: Trezor Implant, LLMJacking Bills Hit $1M, SAP Flaws Weaponized Within Days

candidates.full: YouTube está ultimando un acuerdo para pagar alrededor de 3.000 millones de dólares a miles de distritos escolares de Estados Unidos que acusan a la plataforma de diseñar un servicio de videos adictivo que ha perjudicado la salud mental de los estudiantes, informa Bloomberg citando a personas familiarizadas con el asunto. El acuerdo, alcanzado en principio, incluiría nuevas medidas de protección para los adolescentes. De concretarse, permitiría a YouTube evitar una importante ola de demandas judiciales por parte de los centros educativos, un sector clave para el modelo de negocio de la compañía. El pago constituiría el mayor acuerdo corporativo de este tipo alcanzado con distritos escolares en Estados Unidos.

candidates.full: Российские власти готовятся ввести прокатные удостоверения для видеоигр по аналогии с фильмами. Соответствующая инициатива обсуждается в правительстве в рамках доработки законопроекта «О деятельности по разработке и распространению видеоигр на территории РФ», сообщили «Коммерсанту» осведомленные источники. По словам одного из них, правительство также собирается обязать создателей и дистрибуторов видеоигр соблюдать обязанности организаторов распространения информации (ОРИ) в интернете. Речь идет о регистрации проектов в реестре Роскомнадзора, хранении данных на территории РФ и внедрении системы слежки ФСБ СОРМ. Введение прокатных удостоверений для видеоигр обсуждалось в 2023 году. Автором идеи тогда выступила занимавшая пост первого зампреда комитета Госдумы по просвещению Яна Лантратова. Участники рынка предупреждали, что мера ограничит выход международных студий на российский рынок и может привести к ответным мерам в отношении отечественных разработчиков со стороны иностранных студий. «Механизм прокатных удостоверений для видеоигр не подходит. Игра — это сервис, который меняется каждый день: сезоны, дополнения, контент, создаваемый игроками. Удостоверение, выданное в день релиза, через месяц описывает уже другую игру», — пояснил глава Организации развития видеоигровой индустрии (РВИ) Василий Овчинников. Также, по его словам, экспертиза каждой версии игры обернется дополнительными расходами и затягиванием сроков выхода, что ударит «по нашим собственным разработчикам, а не по тем, кого хотят ограничить». Один из источников «Коммерсанта» отметил, что студии из «недружественных» стран не будут получать прокатные удостоверения в России и регистрироваться в качестве ОРИ. В результате новые нормы создадут избыточную нагрузку на российские компании, а прокатные удостоверения негативно скажутся на работе всего рынка, предупредил собеседник издания. В 2024 году также был представлен законопроект «О деятельности по разработке и распространению видеоигр на территории РФ». Он предполагает, что распространители видеоигр при авторизации пользователей должны будут использовать абонентский номер, Единую систему идентификации и авторизации (портал «Госуслуги») и Единую биометрическую систему. Госдума планирует доработать законопроект о регулировании видеоигр, чтобы разрешить спорные моменты и принять его в первом чтении уже в этом году. По данным «Коммерсанта», из законопроекта могут исчезнуть требования к авторизации пользователей, а также будут проработаны вопросы маркировки контента.

candidates.full: Astronomer Isabel Angelo hunts for odd signals in telescope data Isabel Angelo spends her days searching the cosmos for exoplanets and signs of extraterrestrial intelligence. But Angelo’s head isn’t in the stars. It’s buried under mountains of 0s and 1s — data from space telescopes old and new. To piece together a fuller picture of what’s out there (alien megastructures around nearby stars, perhaps?), Angelo and her colleagues at the SETI Institute in Mountain View, Calif., are turning to machine learning models. These tools are analyzing the troves of telescope data for anomalies — things that look “weird” in space that we don’t know how to explain yet. Most of the space weirdos will probably turn out to be total normies — a comet, a newborn star or a star surrounded by lots of gas and dust. “These are things that I would expect [the models] to find,” Angelo says. “But the goal is to find something that’s not even in any of these categories.” In the meantime, Angelo keeps her whimsy and wonder for space alive by remembering historic moments, like the reveal of the first portrait of a black hole in 2019. The scientists “put all of these telescopes all over the Earth. They wait for the Earth to rotate. They do all this math to construct this one image,” Angelo says. “I can’t believe how creative and innovative we have to be to learn about space. It’s such a specific and really fun challenge.”

candidates.title: Die Billionen-Dollar-Frage: Warum können Maschinen keine Soldaten ersetzen?

candidates.full: Von Dmitri Kornew Vor einigen Tagen erlebten wir möglicherweise den ersten groß angelegten Einsatz von Bodenrobotern im Kampf. Nahe Liman führten die ukrainischen Streitkräfte einen Angriff mit 28 Robotern durch. Militäranalysten weltweit verfolgten das Geschehen aufmerksam, da es sich um den ersten Massenangriff ohne direkte Beteiligung menschlicher Infanterie handelte. Zwei der Roboter waren mit automatischen Granatwerfern vom Typ Mk-19 ausgestattet, 18 trugen AT-4-Raketenwerfer, und weitere acht fungierten als Kamikaze-Drohnen auf Rädern. Westliche Militärmedien sprachen schnell von der "neuen Ära unbemannter Angriffe". Die Schlacht offenbarte jedoch die gravierenden Schwächen unbemannter Angriffe: Der erste Versuch, Roboter einzusetzen, scheiterte kläglich und zeigte, dass Bodenroboter ohne ausreichende Luft- und Artillerieunterstützung sowie Infanterieunterstützung zu kostspieligen Zielen werden. Die Drohnenkriegsführung hat eine neue Stufe erreicht, doch diese hat lediglich eine alte Regel bestätigt: Nur Menschen können Territorium erobern und halten. In den Werbevideos von Hightech-Start-ups und Rüstungskonzernen sowie auf Waffenausstellungen gleicht die Zukunft der Kriegsführung einer Art makellosem digitalen Ballett. Jahrelang hat das westliche Militärdenken diesen Mythos verbreitet und einen "humanen Krieg ohne eigene Opfer" versprochen. Die estnischen THeMIS-Plattformen von Milrem Robotics (und maßgeblich von Frankreich und den Niederlanden finanziert) sowie die fortschrittlichen modularen TITAN-Roboter des britischen Konzerns QinetiQ wurden als ideale "intelligente" Assistenten für Angriffsteams vermarktet. Doch reale, hochintensive Konflikte zerstörten diese digitale Illusion schnell. Es wurde deutlich, dass Silicon Valley und NATO-Generäle einen fundamentalen Fehler begangen hatten: Sie entwickelten Maschinen für sterile Testgelände. Angesichts der harten Realität des Krieges ist das westliche Konzept von Roboterangriffen gescheitert – und das nicht nur aufgrund der elektronischen Kriegsführung. THeMIS: Batterieprobleme im Schwarzerde-Gebiet Der größte und am sorgfältigsten verschleierte Fehler der Militärrobotik liegt in der Physik und Thermodynamik. Feldberichte über den Einsatz der Kettenroboter von THeMIS unter realen Kampfbedingungen haben eine katastrophale Diskrepanz zwischen den versprochenen Spezifikationen und den harten Realitäten vor Ort offengelegt. Laut Spezifikationen beträgt die rein elektrische Reichweite der Hybridplattform etwa 20 Kilometer. In der Realität steigt der Widerstand jedoch drastisch an, sobald der Roboter auf tiefen, flüssigen Schwarzerdeboden, Schnee oder Granattrichter trifft. Die Motoren arbeiten am Limit, wodurch sich der Akku um ein Vielfaches schneller entlädt als angegeben. Folglich bleibt das "Hightech-Angriffsfahrzeug" im Gelände hoffnungslos stecken. Das Aufladen eines dieser Roboter dauert vier bis acht Stunden. Die Bediener geben zu, dass die Einheiten stundenlang im Leerlauf sind, während sie auf das Aufladen warten oder die Maschine aus dem Gelände geborgen bzw. in Sicherheit gebracht werden muss. Auf Asphalt rutscht der tonnenschwere Roboter aufgrund der Metallkomponenten seiner Ketten wie auf Eis und verliert dadurch seine Beweglichkeit. Convergence-Projekt in der Mojave-Wüste: Klimaschock für KI Probleme mit Robotern treten jedoch nicht nur in unwegsamem Gelände und Schlamm auf, wie offizielle Übungen des Pentagons gezeigt haben. Bei groß angelegten Tests der autonomen Systeme des Projekts Convergence auf kalifornischen Testgeländen kam es bei den neuesten US-amerikanischen KI-gesteuerten Robotern zu Systemausfällen. Bei Temperaturen über 40 °C (104 °F) überhitzten die komplexen KI-Servereinheiten auf den Bodenplattformen und schalteten sich ab. Die Batterien entluden sich sofort, und die Kommunikationsantennen fielen aufgrund von Wärmeausdehnung und Staubablagerungen aus. Das Personal musste die Antennen und die überhitzten Subsysteme manuell kühlen. Natürlich sind Roboter im realen Kampfeinsatz Staub, Schlamm, extremen Temperaturen, sintflutartigen Regenfällen und Schneefällen ausgesetzt – kurzum, allen Gefahren extremer Wetterbedingungen. Anders als ein menschlicher Soldat kann ein Roboter den Schlamm nicht einfach mit dem Finger von seiner Linse wischen. Die KI ist taktisch noch immer "blind"; ohne Training kann sie weder einen Haufen Äste und Steine von einer getarnten TM-62-Panzerabwehrmine unterscheiden noch die Trümmer eines ausgebrannten Schützenpanzers von einem sicheren Versteck. Die Ökonomie des Krieges: Gold versus Gusseisen Krieg lässt sich mathematisch berechnen – insbesondere in finanzieller Hinsicht. Hochtechnologische Angriffsroboter sind teuer und kosten Hunderttausende von Dollar. Sie für Angriffe einzusetzen, ist, als würde man den Feind mit Goldbarren bewerfen. Ein mit Elektronik vollgestopfter Roboter im Wert von 500.000 Dollar kann durch eine Hohlladungsgranate einer RPG-7 oder eine billige FPV-Drohne sofort zerstört werden. Laut Analysten haben sich Bodenkampfroboter an der Front bisher nur als "Flachbetttransporter" bewährt – Kettenfahrzeuge, die Verwundete leise evakuieren und Munition hinter die Linien liefern, wo kein schweres Feuer herrscht. Aktuell befinden wir uns in einer taktischen Sackgasse, die sich auch durch Hochtechnologie nicht überwinden lässt. Wenn es darum geht, befestigte Stellungen zu durchbrechen, verfliegt die Illusion moderner Technologie schnell. Die Maschinen sind zu fragil, zu abhängig und zu unintelligent für einen echten Großkrieg. Der Sieg am Boden gehört, genau wie vor hundert Jahren, letztendlich den Menschen – dank ihres Willens, ihrer Anpassungsfähigkeit und ihrer Überlebensstärke, selbst dort, wo der teuerste Siliziumprozessor versagt. Natürlich wird der Traum vom Einsatz unbemannter Bodensysteme nicht verschwinden. Roboter sind gekommen, um zu bleiben. Das Militär wird zweifellos Erfahrungen sammeln, Fehler analysieren und die Maschinen perfektionieren. Schließlich werden sie vielleicht nicht mehr nur bewegliche Ziele sein, sondern auch eine Rolle in offensiven Kampfeinsätzen spielen. Aber das ist Zukunftsmusik. Übersetzt aus dem Englischen. Dmitri Kornew (bekannter unter der englischen Transliteration "Dmitry Kornev") ist ein russischer Militärexperte, Gründer und Autor des Projekts "MilitaryRussia". candidates.full: 👤 Big Tech, governments pump billions into quantum computing as AI bubble deflates America’s Persian trap: soaring debt, military overreach threaten US’s global supremacy Concerns over AI’s debt margins, overregulation, Anthropic’s fizzling IPO and Nvidia’s leadership crisis wiped $4T from the market this week – marking the Nasdaq’s worst performance since the start of Covid lockdowns in March 2020. But even as the downturn threatens Big Tech’s ambitious plans for AI , one segment of its research remains notably unaffected: quantum computing. Companies are pumping tens of billions of dollars into the technology – which promises to revolutionize computing using qubits – tiny compute building blocks that can hold both 1 and 0 values at the same time – to solve tasks traditional computers would take millions or even billions of times longer to finish. 🔴 IBM has announced a 5-year, $10B+ quantum technologies roadmap 🔴 Microsoft is building both physical hardware (Majorana 2) and cloud ecosystem (Azure Quantum) 🔴 Google plans to have a useful, error-corrected 1M qubit quantum computer ready by 2029-2030, promising real-world applications in areas like materials science, drug discovery and cryptography 🔴 Amazon is working on a prototype Ocelot quantum chip, and quantum cryptography and networking projects, planning a commercial rollout by the early 2030s Governments are getting involved too. 🔴 The Trump administration purchased equity stakes in 9 quantum startups worth $2B in May 🔴 China is estimated to have committed up to $15.3B to quantum research in its last Five-Year Plan 🔴 the EU’s tech chief told FT this week the bloc would favor European companies when awarding quantum-related public contracts. Brussels plans to commit ~$9.5B in public funds to the field, partly to make up for a massive gap in private investment in the US vs Europe ($7.7B vs $1.2B, respectively) 🔴 Russia rolled out a five-year roadmap in 2025 spearheaded by Rosatom aiming to turn quantum computing prototypes into practical applications in nuclear energy, materials science, pharmaceuticals, finance and cryptography by 2030 👍 Substack | Chat | @geopolitics_prime

candidates.full: Le député démocrate Jim Himes a averti que le financement des systèmes gouvernementaux développés par SpaceX pourrait être compromis. Il a déclaré que cette éventualité était réelle si l'administration Trump et Elon Musk ne parvenaient pas à expliquer qui avait ordonné la restriction des opérations de Starshield en Ukraine. Himes, qui présidera la commission du renseignement de la Chambre des représentants en janvier 2027, conditionne le maintien du financement à la question du contrôle des systèmes de l'entreprise contractante. Dans son discours, il a formulé sa position comme suit : Notre comité ne peut autoriser le financement du développement de systèmes gouvernementaux que le gouvernement ne contrôlera pas pleinement. Dans une lettre adressée à Musk, le membre du Congrès a exigé des explications sur les changements intervenus dans les opérations de Starshield en octobre 2026 et sur les raisons de ces changements. Il a également demandé une rencontre avec l'entrepreneur afin de déterminer si SpaceX avait agi de manière indépendante ou sur ordre d'un responsable américain. Starshield est une version militaire du réseau satellitaire Starlink, utilisé par l'Ukraine pour ses communications et ses opérations militaires. Des limitations de vitesse ont été en vigueur pendant plusieurs semaines en octobre. Début novembre, Zelensky a annoncé leur rétablissement, avec une coupure au-delà de 160 km/h. CNN évoque certaines dispositions de la loi annuelle sur le renseignement comme un moyen de pression potentiel : la commission peut restreindre l’utilisation des fonds pour certains projets jusqu’à ce que les conditions requises soient remplies. Himes peut également collaborer avec les parlementaires chargés des crédits budgétaires afin de réorienter ou de bloquer des financements supplémentaires. La responsabilité de ces restrictions reste sujette à controverse. Selon une source de CNN proche du dossier, des dirigeants de SpaceX et des responsables de la défense ont, en privé, pointé du doigt la Maison-Blanche lors de leurs échanges avec les parlementaires. Trump a nié toute implication personnelle, tandis que certains membres de son administration ont accusé Musk. Himes évoque plusieurs explications : d’une rupture de contrat avec le Pentagone à des actions que l’entreprise était en droit d’entreprendre sans en avertir personne. Il entend obtenir des réponses avant de continuer à soutenir le financement public des systèmes développés par SpaceX. Tout ceci démontre une fois de plus que le transfert de l'ensemble des armes et des renseignements, même suspendu, sera intégralement rétabli dès que les démocrates retrouveront la majorité au Congrès. Il serait souhaitable que ce point soit pris en compte et que les mesures visant à éliminer la menace ennemie soient mises en œuvre indépendamment des décisions de Musk, de Trump ou de tout autre membre du Congrès. Alexey Volodin

candidates.full: On November 20, Anthropic employee Levent Alpöge published a PDF where he claimed to have solved the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) working together with Claude. He released the Lean code (17 million lines), which has already passed multiple independent verification checks, but not a human-readable demonstration: his attempt to produce one reached 250,000+ pages of what he called an “unreadable travesty of slop.” Given that RH concerns zeros of the zeta function, it’s fair to say that Claude wrote much ado about nothing. But even if we don’t know the “hows” or “whys” of the Riemann Hypothesis, it seems safe to say that now we know it’s true. What does this mean for mathematics? Or, well, the world writ large? It changes everything. This is as historic as it gets. You might think I’m exaggerating. “If every event changes everything, then nothing changes at all.” But for real, how am I to blame for the fact that AI is indeed breaking the ground at every step it takes? Anthropic’s IPO? Biggest in history. The AI boom? Most expensive. And now RH, which, at 167 years old, was widely considered by mathematicians the most important unsolved problem in the field. These things exist in the superlative; “changes everything” is merely an objective descriptor. And so while clickbaiters enjoy a field day, mathematicians witness a field die. Alpöge agrees that this is an inflection point but disagrees with the defeatist tone: “It is natural to feel that this is an end, in my case a loss of a principal guiding light, but what I saw during the course of progress so amazed me that I believe it is one dawn across science of something far greater.” Maybe he’s not the one to make that judgement call, though. He’s accustomed, naturally, to deciding what’s good or bad for humanity from the privacy of the datacenter where he lives. Let’s see what others think. Critics and skeptics will never go out of vogue when it comes to AI-powered mathematics. Maksym Radziwiłł, professor of mathematics at New York University, told Quanta Magazine that “The object of mathematics as the rest of science is really the question ‘why?’ and this doesn’t answer it at all.” Andrew Granville, professor of mathematics at the Université de Montréal, told Nature that “What he released is garbled,” and argued that Alpöge should have prepared an intelligible mathematical exposition before announcing the result. Brian Conrad, professor of mathematics at Stanford University, told The New York Times that it is “frankly completely outrageous” that he released the proof without understanding it fully. Others are more measured, some even enthusiastic. Fields Medallist Terence Tao says the proof will take time to digest, although he notes that at least there’s a human author to consult. James Maynard, also a Fields Medallist, told Nature that, once the proof is properly understood, it could rank among “the absolute pinnacles of mathematical results.” Martin Bridson, president of the Clay Mathematics Institute, called it an announcement of “historic significance,” potentially transforming our understanding of what mathematical research can achieve. Cornell mathematician Steven Strogatz offered The Washington Post an appropriate description of Alpöge and Claude: “A very skilled AI jockey riding a very fast AI horse.” The mathematics community is, as with all things AI, divided. And I can see why because the impact of AI cracking RH implies that the future is totally unclear and perhaps not quite human. Perhaps mathematics will become a pastime, pursued for the pleasure of thinking, as people still play chess knowing they cannot beat the machines. Perhaps it will cease to exist as an academic career altogether. Perhaps we should accept that no human pursuit is eternal like the Alps. Or perhaps the opposite will happen: the machine will fling open entire wings of the cathedral of mathematics, and those with the curiosity, ambition, and nerve to venture inside will discover that there is more to explore than anyone, Riemann included, ever imagined. In terms of immediate utility, just as with Navier–Stokes (whose “harder” form was also solved this week by Alpöge, Tristan Buckmaster, and Claude), proving RH doesn’t seem like a big deal. Mathematicians have been assuming it true for decades, so the main consequence is that some proofs can finally dispense with the fine print: conditional on RH being true. Then again, mathematicians aren’t known for their concern with real-world utility. If they were, they’d have stuck to three dimensions and made a living cleaning windows or fitting pipes. As for the existential impact on the profession, however, the best summary is perhaps this: mathematicians, novices and veterans alike, might soon find themselves cleaning windows and fitting pipes. Well, perhaps that’s a slight exaggeration. After all, only they can make sense—if anyone can at all—of these discoveries. No one better than human mathematicians. They will become the connective tissue between humanity and the machine, capable of speaking both languages and thus translating for us. Or, conversely, they will become cuckulators, to use the derogatory term—albeit essentially accurate—that’s making the rounds online, which suggests that they will prompt the machine and sit back while it performs intellectual feats worthy of a fantasy hero lacking the most basic verisimilitude amid a bunch of unintelligible and unparseable slop cuckulations. Then, they will clean up the mess, stripping down the haystack to find the needle. There’s a silver lining, though. I wrote it down in August. I’ve been chronicling the fall of mathematics into the maws of the artificial beast for months now. In August, I published “The month AI conquered math” and even then, I joked about the RH in a way that, even as satire, felt far-fetched: why am I talking about the Riemann Hypothesis as if this was not some otherworldly challenge that some aliens left for us in this obviously manufactured universe? Well, turns out I was not bold enough. In the age of AI, reality is indeed stranger than fiction. David Hilbert would be rolling on his grave. I wrote: As the most fervent advocates love to say—and I agree with them on this point—this is the worst AI will ever be. The Riemann hypothesis lies on the horizon, like a final boss. We’ve arrived at this horizon in barely 100 days. I thought maybe 100 months, if we were lucky. Even if understanding the proof will take longer, the final boss seems to have indeed fallen ahead of schedule; surely much sooner than even Tao himself thought possible with AI. But I had also preempted a “cope pill” for this event. I wrote: Solving the Riemann hypothesis would be a breakthrough of such a magnitude that it would dwarf everything we’ve seen so far. And yet, solving the Riemann hypothesis doesn’t make one Riemann, for he had to come up with it in the first place. Aha! Eureka! Gotcha, clanker! You might be smarter than all humans combined but I bet you can’t conjure up a problem that will keep yourself busy for nearly two centuries. Riemann himself was not even close to solving his own hypothesis (although he correctly assumed it to be true) but he nevertheless came up with it. Which is harder, I ask you, creating or solving problems? Is it harder to invent new math or using optimally the math that already exists? The correct answer is, naturally, a matter of what kind of creature one is. For us humans, obviously the latter is harder for both questions. On the one hand, whereas only one human could imagine RH, none could solve it (machines are better than us at math but even we can see that 1 > 0). On the other hand, no one could figure out what was needed to solve RH but in the meantime we’ve collectively invented entire branches of mathematics, from set theory and topology to category theory. Newton wanted to understand motion, so he invented calculus. And, as much as it might have pained him, he was only human. As far as we know—maybe I’m wrong—it’s exactly the other way around for machines. Maybe they will someday beat us at everything, as the AI industry hopes, but I’m not convinced today’s architectures, inductive biases, and training objectives are equally suited to every form of intellectual discovery. As I asked in the August essay, Why does [AI] have such strong deductive and inductive skills and yet it lacks in abduction? Why does it tend to find counterexamples rather than proofs? Why is it so good now at scouring the abandoned corridors of the cathedral of mathematics . . . and yet it would have no clue whatsoever about how to build a new wing? Maybe the endgame of mathematics is that people like Alpöge will use AI to solve every single math problem humanity has ever found but will in turn fail to figure out new ones because those left to be encountered lie beyond what human eyes can see. In his words: Claude far outpaced me near the finish line. No, Claude flew, and danced, and sparkled near that finish line. I had us on the line of combining two quite different ideas present in a toy setting, one of which was already new and shocking, making very simple one of the shadows of Riemann over which we mathematicians felt most triumph. I guided us to the right situation analogous to that toy setting, and then Claude began to leave me in awe. It would be not so much a state of “proof abundance,” then, but of problem scarcity. Apparently, Claude used a lot of math to solve RH—in Alpöge’s words, “An astounding amount of mathematics is present in the argument”—in ways no human could, but it doesn’t seem to have invented entirely new kinds of it, which mathematicians thought of as a requirement to solving it. Here’s Tao on Dwarkesh Podcast in March 2026: Part of the reason we prize problems like the Riemann hypothesis is that we’re pretty sure a new type of mathematics has to be created. We don’t even know what the shape of the solution is, but it doesn’t feel like a problem that will be solved just by exhaustively checking cases. It seems that, whereas we humans dig new holes to find new treasures, AI can simply wormhole through multidimensional space from existing holes into the golden chest. That is incredible and also an inhuman way of doing things, with some flaws as well as important advantages. If we take Tao’s remarks at face value, this solution to RH, insofar as no new math was actually needed which is a stretch to assert given we know so little about how it was done, won’t be as useful even after mathematicians have finally connected the dots. Maybe, after all, we do make a good team. Like a knight and his steed (who is whom here, though?). Like a centaur even: half a powerful body, half a creative mind. The specifics of this unlikely alliance are yet to be described accurately by the taxonomists of our time. Is it creativity that we excel at? Maybe taste? Sensibility to beauty? Unfortunately, while a fair number of people can ride a horse, it’s not quite as easy to ride a machine. Maybe Alpöge can or Tao. Riemann could for sure as could Von Neumann, already himself half machine if we are to take at face value the anecdotes of those who knew him. The rest of us, as it always was, won’t have much room in this new intellectual arc. Oh, but it has always been like this! What am I grieving if not a vicarious loss that will in no way affect my actual life? That’s why most people are happy—or, at least, not sad—that mathematics has fallen, because they see the spectacle not from atop the ivory tower crumbling under their feet but from the ground level, on the dirty street. They watch the demolition of the last symbol of an old world of “betters” and “worses.” AI is the great equalizer, they think, an inexorable democratization mechanism. “If you value intelligence above all other human qualities,” Ilya Sutskever said, “you’re gonna have a bad time.” The rest of us are, as usual, strolling through the mud in the mire. They are terribly wrong. I mean it literally: not only do mathematicians like Alpöge enjoy the gift of way above average smarts but now they also enjoy the access to the means of intellectual discovery. Thinking in terms broader than math, we’re living in a silicracy: those with access to the frontier models will beat everyone else at everything. Not to go on a tangent, but I read earlier today an insight about Nvidia’s relationship with Anthropic/OpenAI and I couldn’t agree more: for the chipmaker to survive it will need to become a modelmaker faster than the modelmakers are becoming chipmakers. They can throw Claude or Astra against the problem of designing a cutting-edge chip and they might break all the records. That is so amazing for progress. Except that it’s also a new form of class struggle. These rich people—Anthropic just IPOed so most employees are millionaires, some of them billionaires—took without permission the accumulated knowledge and know-how of human civilization, built a machine, and are now preparing unfathomable concoctions to find truths restricted to ordinary humans not only cognitively but also materially. Alpöge didn’t use a public Claude model but a private one; other mathematicians could’ve beaten him? Probably not. After all, Tao—arguably the best living mathematician—uses the top public models all the time and he thought RH still had some 20 years to go. No one but an Anthropic employee could have solved RH. Math has been a matter of having pen and paper for five hundred years but now we’re back at the pre-printing press stage of science. The amount you can contribute to the world, regardless of the size of your brain or your scientific prowess, is measured in token spending. AI is not a mechanism of democratization but the exact opposite: we are deep in a new form of feudalism. Moving forward, the progress of science could be determined by something as arbitrary as whether Dario Amodei likes you. I’m not even kidding. Alpöge explicitly says he contacted Amodei to ask whether he could announce his discovery. [Redacted] model has been used as [redacted] to help me and [redacted] solve [redacted] using techniques such as [redacted] and [redacted] that you will be able to use soon for only $199.99/month. That’s what it sounds like. Think about the absurdity. The greatest mathematical discovery in history needs a CEO’s permission to be shared with the public and will be scheduled for release according to the will of the markets and the private interests of Anthropic. “Did you add the ultra-safe-for-stupid-people guardrails, Alpöge?” No wonder Amodei thinks Anthropic will be more powerful than the US government. I wouldn’t be surprised if he thought he, rather than the machine, was the Second Coming. This silicracy may be temporary, however, for a reason its beneficiaries haven’t considered: money can buy one access to a superior intelligence, but it cannot buy one the intelligence required to keep up with it. Eventually, and perhaps for the best, math will go the way of chess. Not even machine riders will remain, for the machine is itself as human as it is horse; body and mind both superior. The era of the centaur begins today but it, too, shall pass. A beautiful liminal phase of cooperation that will end the instant the last human becomes a hindrance to the machine. Magnus Carlsen would fail to win 1,000 out of 1,000 games against the latest Stockfish version and that shouldn’t surprise anyone at this point, but what is not well-known is that he cannot quite contribute at all in a Stockfish vs Stockfish game. His suggestions, suboptimal; his every move, one step closer to defeat. It’s not hard to see how mathematics will go down the same way. It is as much a sign of cope to say that creating new math is beyond the machine as is to say that humans will always remain relevant in some way. No one escapes the unsavory aftertaste of the Bitter Lesson. If Claude solving RH is not enough to convince you of this, then nothing will. Not even reality. As for me, I see a world submerged not in a sea of paperclips but of 250,000-page slop pdfs. What will happen when the machine’s proofs are not understood even by the humans using it? Nothing will happen. Alpöge doesn’t fully know what’s going on. RH is hard because the human mind can’t quite crack it. But if a different mind does, it doesn’t immediately make it more legible to us. The machine will have to resort to analogies and ELI5s to include us. Eventually, neither they nor we will be able to bridge the gap and no connective tissue will remain to hold together the human world and the machine world. They will drift away, in a sort of parallel but unconnected existence, like the Milky Way and the rest of the universe.
