candidates.title: Armenia's AI Silk Road aims to reconnect East and West
candidates.summary: With a new computing power centre, international collaborations and a robotics lab, the small South Caucasus country seeks to turn its technological talent into greater economic influence. The ancient Silk Road carried goods, knowledge and ideas between East and West. In Armenia, tech industry leade
candidates.full: With a new computing power centre, international collaborations and a robotics lab, the small South Caucasus country seeks to turn its technological talent into greater economic influence. The ancient Silk Road carried goods, knowledge and ideas between East and West. In Armenia, tech industry leaders are re-imagining it in the modern day: a network linking countries through the infrastructure needed to develop artificial intelligence. "What we are starting to rebuild is the ancient Silk Road," said Rev Lebaredian, vice president of NVIDIA responsible for physical AI simulation, speaking at the DigiTec Technology Conference in Yerevan. "It is coming back, but in this new form, as a kind of AI Silk Road," he said. He argued that Armenia and Kazakhstan can become its main pillars, with countries in the region contributing at different levels of the AI economy: energy, microprocessors, computing infrastructure, models and applications. The vision goes beyond constructing data centres. It is about connecting markets, researchers, businesses and capital across borders, and creating a role for smaller economies in an industry dominated by much larger powers. "We must work hard to create as much interdependence between us as possible," Lebaredian said. "That will help everyone’s prosperity and strengthen our security." The emerging corridor is starting to take physical shape. Firebird, a US-based AI infrastructure company with Armenian co-founders, opened a computing centre in Armenia in August and is building another one in Kazakhstan. With more than 6,100 NVIDIA Blackwell processors, the Armenian facility provides the computing power businesses need to train and run artificial intelligence systems. NVIDIA itself is among its clients, while Perplexity also collaborates with it, linking the small country with international AI players. A small country looking beyond its borders This ambition runs through the DigiTec Conference, held from 20 to 22 November at Yerevan’s Meridian Expo Center. The organisers announced 125 speakers, including representatives of NVIDIA, OpenAI, Dell Technologies and Mozilla, bringing international technology companies together with governments and entrepreneurs from the region. For Armenia’s technology community, the event is also a space to showcase the position the country wants to secure. Armen Kocharyan, president of the Union of Advanced Technology Enterprises UATE, which organises DigiTec, described it as a "live platform" that connects governments, investors and businesses from Europe, the Gulf, Central Asia and North America". "A real hub never stops at borders. [...] We promote all five layers of artificial intelligence together, connecting people, technology, capital and markets in real time," Kocharyan said. "We are creating a live platform" that brings together governments, investors and businesses from Europe, the Gulf, Central Asia and North America so they can develop technology, invest and expand their activities." For a country of around three million people, these connections are essential. Armenia’s domestic market cannot by itself support the growth of an AI industry. The opportunity lies in specialisation and cooperation with neighbours and partners, members of the Armenian technology community stress. 7% of national GDP The political interest is also clear: the DigiTec programme includes a discussion between Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan and Nvidia's Lebaredian on turning the vision of an AI hub into reality. The country is building on an already developed technology sector. Arto Minasyan, co-founder of AI companies Krisp and 10Web and an investor in new technology ventures, said the sector makes up 7% of the Armenian economy, and described an ecosystem with its own unicorns, investment funds and research labs. "The dream of building a technologically advanced Armenia pushed me to found the company and move from academic research into entrepreneurship," said Minasyan. "It pushed my co-founder David to come back from Silicon Valley and start the company. It pushed many researchers from leading universities to come to Armenia and join forces to build here," he added. This international network is a key element of the strategy. The Armenian diaspora provides connections through which know-how, information and business opportunities can flow. The advice to build a supercomputer The first tentative steps towards attracting Nvidia to Armenia also had a personal motivation. Lebaredian described how, after he set up Nvidia's office in Moscow in 2004, he began dreaming of something similar for Armenia, waiting for the right conditions to emerge. The Armenian office opened in 2022. Today it employs more than 100 people, he says. But attracting an international technology company was only one part of the ambition. The bigger question was how Armenian researchers and entrepreneurs would get the tools needed to develop technology themselves. Lebaredian recounted a meeting at Nvidia's California headquarters in 2019, when Pashinyan asked the company’s co-founder Jensen Huang what Armenia should do to attract a company like Nvidia. According to Lebaredian, the answer was to build an AI supercomputer for its people. He said that initial efforts to secure state funding were halted by the pandemic and the war. The commercial project later took shape, as partners, capital and clients came together, with DigiTec 2024 serving as a meeting point. This journey matters, because Armenia’s proposal relies on more than access to imported chips. The country has a tradition in computing dating back to the Soviet era, as well as expertise in semiconductor design and in the software used to develop them. Armenia’s Minister of High-Tech Industry and Artificial Intelligence, David Tadevosyan, focused on the same challenge: how to turn successes in software and technology services into domestic research, engineering and production of internationally competitive products. He highlighted human capital, modern infrastructure and cooperation between science and business as the necessary conditions. The minister said the government had approved, around two weeks before DigiTec, an educational programme in physical artificial intelligence, involving international-level experts. The aim, he explained, is for technological development to boost the productivity and competitiveness of the entire economy. Firebird: The "AI factory" and expansion into Kazakhstan Firebird’s facility in Hrazdan is the most visible expression of this strategy. An AI factory provides the computing power businesses need to train and run artificial intelligence systems, without having to build their own data centres. Speaking to Euronews, Firebird co-founder and CEO Razmig Hovaghimian described a project that from the outset was driven by an ambition to go beyond the country’s borders. "Why build it only in Armenia? Why not build it with Armenia as a starting point, expand it globally and attract talent and investment here?" he said. An Armenian originally from Egypt with experience in creating and selling tech businesses, he saw in AI an opportunity to tap the country’s human capital. Implementing it, however, required more than good engineers: funding, licences to export US technology and investors’ trust in a market they were not used to associating with such large-scale infrastructure. "We knew we had the talent. We just had to convince the rest of the world that this is the right place to build and grow," he said. According to Hovaghimian, the first phase has around 6,200 GPUs, while demand was for about 25,000. "Everyone was saying that perhaps we would have one customer who would take all the capacity. We have 15," he said, adding that 12 of them are Armenian companies. The customers he named include Nvidia and Perplexity, as well as Krisp and Activeloop. The presence of domestic firms shows that the facility can also serve as infrastructure for the local ecosystem, beyond serving international clients. The second phase is already under construction, he said, with the aim of bringing the infrastructure in Armenia to around 70,000 GPUs in 2027. "Today we are at 6,200. We are already building the second phase. Next year we will be at around 70,000," he told Euronews. The expansion into Kazakhstan fits the same logic: developing infrastructure in markets that have talent and business potential but need access to AI computing power. Hovaghimian put Firebird’s broader international plan at around two to two and a half gigawatts, with additional markets under exploration. Firebird’s ambition, he stressed, is to give more countries the ability to develop their own technology. "Not simply to become passive consumers of AI, but to take an active part in creating it." An entire country as an AI laboratory For Lebaredian, computing infrastructure is the starting point for the next step, "physical artificial intelligence" that involves robots, autonomous vehicles and systems that operate in the real world after being trained and tested in simulations. He sees applications from agriculture and manufacturing to health and transport, sectors that account for a large part of the global economy. In Armenia, a new robotics and physical intelligence lab links universities, the state and businesses to develop researchers and practical applications. "To turn the whole country into our laboratory and our industries into a lab," he proposed, referring to mines, agriculture and high-tech production such as drones. In his view, Armenia’s small size can make cooperation easier and speed up the move from research to deployment. That is where the success of the new Silk Road will be decided: in the country’s ability to turn computing power into home-grown businesses and technologies.

candidates.summary: У суперфіналі «Фабрики зірок» через 17 років знову прозвучала композиція «Бережи любов». Її виконали учасники нового сезону разом зі Стасом Шурінсом, який долучився до виступу у форматі відеозапису. Один із музичних номерів десятого прайму присвятили приверненню суспільної уваги до теми ВІЛ та СНІДу
candidates.full: У суперфіналі «Фабрики зірок» через 17 років знову прозвучала композиція «Бережи любов». Її виконали учасники нового сезону разом зі Стасом Шурінсом, який долучився до виступу у форматі відеозапису. Один із музичних номерів десятого прайму присвятили приверненню суспільної уваги до теми ВІЛ та СНІДу. Напередодні Всесвітнього дня боротьби зі СНІДом, який відзначають 1 грудня, організатори проєкту спільно з Фондом Олени Пінчук нагадали глядачам про важливість профілактики ВІЛ та своєчасного тестування. Композиція «Бережи любов», яка вперше пролунала на «Фабриці зірок» 17 років тому, отримала нове аранжування. Під час виступу фабрикантів на екранах позаду сцени транслювали заздалегідь записане виконання Стаса Шурінса. Таким чином організатори поєднали виступи представників різних поколінь «Фабрики зірок», зберігши первинний соціальний посил композиції. Нагадаємо, Стас Шурінс є переможцем третього сезону української «Фабрики зірок». Фото: скриншоти випуску шоу «Фабрика зірок» Команда «Детектора медіа» понад 20 років виконує роль watchdog'a українських медіа. Ми аналізуємо якість контенту і спонукаємо медіагравців дотримуватися професійних та етичних стандартів. Щоб інформація, яку отримуєте ви, була правдивою та повною. До 22-річчя з дня народження видання ми відновлюємо нашу Спільноту! Це коло активних людей, які хочуть та можуть фінансово підтримати наше видання, долучитися до генерування спільних ідей та отримувати більше ексклюзивної інформації про стан справ в українських медіа. Мабуть, ще ніколи якісна журналістика не була такою важливою, як сьогодні.

candidates.title: Vibecoding an Inference Chip
candidates.summary: One of the more entertaining things about programming recently is that coding agents let me work in entirely new domains by giving me access to new programming languages and paradigms. Lately, that has meant hacking on hardware, now that writing low-level software is much easier. So, in this blog po
candidates.full: One of the more entertaining things about programming recently is that coding agents let me work in entirely new domains by giving me access to new programming languages and paradigms. Lately, that has meant hacking on hardware, now that writing low-level software is much easier. So, in this blog post, I’m going to try to recount the experience of vibe coding an FPGA, going through a series of “oh shit” moments several times, and giving myself a new appreciation for what’s possible if you have a large token budget (thanks YC) and interesting problems to point the models at. I overheard some founders recently talk about how FPGAs work. I’ll admit I was relatively naive about them. I’d never really experimented with them in my startup or in college, so I knew little about them before. The basic idea I was familiar with: you can program a circuit into a reprogrammable chip. So rather than having a general purpose computing architecture (like a CPU) you can have a reprogrammable one, i.e. the configuration loaded onto the chip determines how its logic and routing are connected, and that (in theory) enables performance advantages. I also know that it took a mountain of C++ to write and involved manually analyzing waveforms for simulation and verification. I had never done this before though and it seemed cumbersome. That’s about what I knew going into this. Naturally, my ML brain thought “could we use these for AI inference”. I’m not the first to think this — there are a few repos attempting to port ML models to FPGAs on Github. But I hadn’t actually seen a writeup on whether coding agents are good at writing the low level C++ and Verilog code to program them and verifying the outputs so that they actually run accurately. (Spoiler alert, they are incredible at programming them.) So I decided I needed to get my hands on one. AWS has F2 instances with FPGA hardware, and that seemed easier than going and buying physical hardware, so I asked Codex to spin up a reservation and got cooking. It had a relatively limited memory of 16 GB of FPGA HBM. Around the same time, I was working with the DeepGrove founders who were discussing their new ternary weight architecture that is well suited for memory limited cases. It’s SOTA on Mac hardware with actual agentic tool calling, so I figured why not, let’s see if I can get this working on an FPGA and fast enough to be useful. What followed was a cloud agent running in Conductor for several days with me mostly just encouraging it periodically while it both (1) got a model fully running and (2) increased its speed by 33× from the first full-model bit-exact baseline to get it to a real-time relevant speed. It was one of the most mind blowing autoresearch loops I’ve run, ultimately writing roughly 3M lines across the experiment history and parsing 30M lines of output files, burning only $10,000 in Claude and OpenAI tokens to run hundreds of experiments. Most of the code is C++ and some Verilog. It’s been probably a decade since the last time I wrote any serious amount of C++ and I’ve never written Verilog. I honestly don’t know the first thing about Verilog. Most of my prompts were not particularly clever: they consisted mostly of me saying things like “you’re a superintelligent model, time to be more creative” and “let’s go for 2x faster, you got this”. Sometimes I brought some ML knowhow like “hey it’s time to consider speculative decoding” or “why is that running on CPU, you should port it”. But for the most part, it was just vibes and I’m pretty sure that with enough time the model would have figured out those things. Also, it seemed that both Astra and Opus (new Fable wasn’t out yet) were pretty capable at this and I could use them interchangeably. I’m sure someone has a good benchmark for which is smarter but both passed my smart-enough threshold. From “it works” to 213 tokens per second The chart follows the measured optimization sequence: 6 → 213 tokens/s, or 33× the baseline. How much did the human advice help? At one point, around when it got to 10 TPS, I messaged the DeepGrove founders about this, and they replied surprised that it was working so easily, saying they had tried this a few months back and the models were not quite good enough to be particularly effective. They sent me a prompt that summarizes some of their lessons and I copy-pasted it into my session to see if it’d matter. It was essentially the most significant piece of actual guidance I added to this session. The prompt is reproduced below. Read the full FPGA design prompt here is what someone else did for a dense bs=1 decode optimized fpga implementation for a dense qwen style model with ternary weights. you should take this with a grain of salt and pick things that you believe are acutally useful to add to your plan. Please also dont do things if you dont think is useful that take a lot of times like runnning really long test of a cycle accurate simulation etc or like physical design since those can take like hours. here are some ideas please pick and choose use this as context and not somehting that you shoudl be strictly guided by somethings that could help. prioritiize speed of like getting this up and running though.. MATMUL (TERNARY ENGINE) - No multipliers. A 2-bit weight drives a 3:1 mux that picks x, ~x, or 0. The unused 4th code raises an error flag, so corrupt weights get caught. - Negation is ~x + 1. Lanes flag negatives, and the row reducer adds the +1s once per row instead of once per lane. - Activations are grouped integers: INT12, or INT16 where we needed more range (MLP down projection). Reduce as integers, apply FP32 group scales, accumulate in FP32. - The pre-projection RMSNorm is deferred: quantize the activation first, apply the normalization scale after accumulation. It’s cheaper and numerically equivalent. - 8 cores in two clusters. Projections that are independent (gate/up) run at the same time on separate core groups. - Result: about half the DSPs of an INT8/INT16 design at the same rate, traded for more LUTs. MEMORY - Weights are packed at 2 bits, 8x more per transfer than 16-bit. At batch 1, weight fetch costs far more energy and time than the math. - Weights stream from HBM straight into the compute lanes and skip the on-chip buffers (they’re used once per token). Activations are cached next to each core and reused across rows. - HBM routing is one chain per memory channel instead of a big crossbar. Lay out data so all 32 channels stay busy. - On-chip buffers are typed slots with an explicit lifecycle (open -> write -> commit -> read -> release). Each slot has a side memory for scales/exponents. The buffer checks format, range and producer, which catches scheduling bugs in hardware. - The KV cache is MXINT8: 8-bit values with one shared exponent per 32-channel block. That’s small enough to stream, with accuracy held. - For MoE: stripe each expert across every channel, and map expert ID to address at runtime instead of using a fixed program. ATTENTION - Attention streams over the cache in 64-token tiles with an online softmax (FP32 running max/sum). The full score matrix is never stored. - Probabilities are UINT16 and the context accumulates in FP32. - Each attention unit interleaves two independent jobs on one datapath (C-slow), which hides pipeline latency without duplicating hardware. - Q/K head norm and RoPE got their own small vector unit, so they don’t block the general vector path. The V projection overlaps with that work. - New K/V is appended to HBM as soon as it’s produced. We used a sliding window to bound cache reads. SCHEDULING - One controller issues work in program order, with tags and barriers. Engines overlap only when the buffer dependencies are explicit, so we got overlap without races. - For MoE: the router is the new critical path, because nothing can fetch until it finishes. Keep it in FP32 (lower precision changed which experts were picked), and overlap whatever you can around it. CORRECTNESS (maybe not neecessary to folow super close) - We fixed a numerics contract first (formats, rounding points, operation order) and built hardware to match it. Vector ops must match the reference model’s order and precision, not just be “close”. - Verification ladder: - Per-block cocotb unit tests. - One full layer co-simulated against the real checkpoint. - Multi-token, full 24-layer decode compared token-for-token with a reference oracle. - Byte-level accounting of KV cache writes. - We kept simulation results, timing signoff and board results separate, and never claimed one from another. - Every published number links to the report it came from. PHYSICAL DESIGN (maybe not necessary for u) - The chip has 3 regions (SLRs). Keep wide datapaths inside one region and register every crossing. Long links use credits, not combinational ready. - We placed engines next to their data: memory logic near HBM, attention in the DSP-dense region. - Screen logic depth (10 levels max at 250 MHz) right after synthesis, and fix it with pipelining, sharding, or C-slow. Full place-and-route is saved for integration. - Dev loop: small change -> lint -> unit test -> quick synthesis -> depth/timing check -> restructure. The coding agent diligently considered these asks, but it didn’t seem to make all that much of a difference qualitatively. Indeed, when I asked it later to read all of the logs and determine which of these instructions it actually used, it said: Read the agent’s retrospective: what it adopted and rejected Its biggest design ideas were already in my plan before you pasted it. You pasted it on Oct 29 at 21:50 UTC: 4,741 characters describing what someone else did for a dense, batch-1, ternary FPGA decoder. Within 70 seconds I had sorted it into ten ideas to adopt and five to reject, and written that into every design agent’s brief. The shorter remark from your friend Edward, about using lookup tables as logic gates, came 24 minutes earlier and left nothing on the speed line. Design ideas I adopted: mostly confirmation. - Already planned: streaming weights straight into the compute lanes, running rows in parallel, and reading the attention cache in bursts were all in the design brief I’d launched 35–40 minutes earlier. - Match what was later built: - interleaved lanes in the router (step 3); - a separate unit for head norms and RoPE (step 4); - a program-order sequencer (step 5); - a registered boundary on every crossing between dies (steps 8 and 12). - I can’t show these wouldn’t have happened without the notes. Ideas I rejected: all five numerics shortcuts. Lower-precision activations, a deferred norm, an 8-bit KV cache, online softmax and 16-bit probabilities each change the output bits. That is where their design got its efficiency, and your bit-exact rule ruled it out. Process advice: this changed things right away. - What you asked: not to do things that take hours. - What I stopped: a simulation that had run for about 24 hours, and two 250 MHz builds. - What I switched to: a short loop of C tests, synthesis and a logic-depth check, with one place-and-route per integration. - Likely gain: it got hardware results sooner. - Possible cost, which I can’t prove: two hangs that only RTL simulation could show reached the board the next day, and the big integration lost 38 hours to them. One real find it triggered. While checking their memory ideas, I found AWS’s own reference memory design, which reaches 426 GB/s across all 32 memory channels. The memory subsystem was built from it. In other words, for most of the actual design ideas it is unclear but there is good reason to believe the model would have figured them out, especially because it came up with them many cycles later after several compaction cycles. But the process advice was useful immediately for getting to hardware results sooner and increasing iteration speed. In other words, the humans are still useful at defining how to iterate fast and what correctness looks like, and the agents are great to manage the exploration. The optimization log Here are the changes the autoresearch loop found. Interestingly, it’s mostly a series of modest improvements that compound 1.5x ish every time, rather than one or two giant ones. 0Baseline6.43 tok/s Baseline: the first full-model bit-exact FPGA image (R8), served with host-side prefix caching. 1.0× from baseline 1Host overhead8.07 tok/s Host software only: per-command overhead fell from ~10 ms to 0.9 ms (persistent register mapping, streaming reads, no per-command SDK calls or fsyncs). 1.25× this step · 1.25× from baseline 2Burst attention14.02 tok/s A 128-lane attention engine that reads the KV cache in bursts instead of a word at a time, keeping the reference's exact summation order. 1.74× this step · 2.18× from baseline 3Parallel router20.53 tok/s A parallel MoE router with an exact GCC-sort tie-breaker plus a streaming output head with built-in argmax; moderate-effort routing let it run at 250 MHz. 1.46× this step · 3.19× from baseline 4Glue engine30.24 tok/s A glue engine that parallelizes norms, RoPE, quantization and copies between engines in certified exact orders. 1.47× this step · 4.70× from baseline 5New pipeline49.21 tok/s The full new pipeline (streaming ternary projection lanes + a new sequencer replacing R8's control path), after fixing two hangs that only appeared in hardware. 1.63× this step · 7.65× from baseline 6Prompt speculation51.25 tok/s Exact speculative decoding: the host drafts tokens by prompt lookup and the FPGA verifies several in one pass. 1.04× this step · 7.97× from baseline 7Router relay58.43 tok/s Fixed a relay that moved router weights between dies at 1/6 speed: router stall per layer 43,862 → 12,292 cycles. 1.14× this step · 9.08× from baseline 8Head shadow94.44 tok/s Head shadow v2 (start the next token on a provisional guess; catch misses early) plus cross-die timing fixes, enabling 237.5 MHz kernel / 450 MHz memory. 1.62× this step · 14.68× from baseline 9Draft model105.63 tok/s Exact speculative decoding with a real draft model: a cut-down Maple on the F2's host CPUs drafts ahead, and the FPGA verifies every token. 1.12× this step · 16.42× from baseline 10Memory ports108.81 tok/s Doubled the memory ports from 4 to 8 (two projection lanes, output head striped across banks): 1.39× per clock, but congestion cut the clock to 181/375 MHz. 1.03× this step · 16.91× from baseline 11Attention overlap134.99 tok/s Hid the attention engine's KV fetches behind its compute, and replaced the router's 2,048-step serial sum with an exact order-independent one (12,292 → 2,338 cycles per layer). 1.24× this step · 20.98× from baseline 12Weight packing171.3 tok/s Lossless 5-trit weight packing (−20% weight bytes), shorter serial steps, and moving the output head to the far die, which relieved congestion and allowed 225/400 MHz. 1.27× this step · 26.63× from baseline 13Re-speculation184.19 tok/s Re-speculation after head-shadow misses, speculative MoE expert prefill during the router, and a die rebalance (without the unused DDR controller) that ran 231.25/450 MHz on both boots. 1.08× this step · 28.63× from baseline 14Parallel head loader213.13 tok/s A head loader that reads both of its memory banks at once (+17.3%, measured on and off on one image), a runtime expert-prefetch policy, and the router-job timing fix; run one clock step lower (225/425 MHz) after a soak test found random faults at 231.25. 1.16× this step · 33.13× from baseline How it compares It’s difficult to do a 1:1 comparison across these configurations. I didn’t run the same autoresearch loop on every alternative, and I assume there is more performance to extract if I did. The point is to show how slow the FPGA was in its first implementation, and how far the optimization loop took it. The measurements below are from November 15 on AWS, replaying the same 8-chat × 3-turn benchmark. Prices are the on-demand rates recorded with that experiment. “Exact turns” counts outputs that matched the pinned CPU reference. The GPU implementations are included for context but did not satisfy the same bit-exact criterion but are pretty close in practice. | What | Instance | Price per hour | Bench tok/s | Exact turns | FPGA is faster by | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | F2 FPGA, r9 (final image) | f2.6xlarge | $1.98 | 213.13 | 24/24 | — | | Exact CPU twin, 32 threads | m8a.8xlarge (32 Zen 5 cores) | $1.95 | 129.5 | 24/24 | 1.65× | | Exact CPU twin, 24 threads | c7i.12xlarge (24 Sapphire Rapids cores) | $2.14 | 99.6 | 24/24 | 2.14× | | Pinned scalar reference, all 32 cores | m8a.8xlarge | $1.95 | 40.6 | 24/24 | 5.25× | | Pinned scalar reference as pinned, 1 thread | r7i.2xlarge | $0.53 | 1.1 | 24/24 | 195× | | Exact CPU twin, 4 threads (small instance) | m8a.xlarge (4 Zen 5 cores) | $0.24 | 67.6 | 24/24 | 3.16× | | DeepGrove’s own fork with GPU offload (not bit-exact, shown for reference) | g4dn.xlarge (T4 GPU) | $0.53 | 35.7 | 1/24 | 5.97× | | Community CUDA port (not bit-exact, shown for reference) | g4dn.xlarge (T4 GPU) | $0.53 | 166.3 | 0/24 | 1.28× | What happens as the context grows? This is one generation starting with a 16-token prompt and continuing until the 8,192-token context is full: 8,176 generated tokens. The five middle columns show decode speed in tokens/s at the indicated context length for several generations of iteration. The last column is wall-clock time for the whole run/ | Image | 16–64 | 1–2k | 2–4k | 4–6k | 6–8k | Whole run (s) | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | r5 | 108 | 70 | 57 | 45 | 37 | 162.3 s | | r6b | 142 | 111 | 90 | 72 | 60 | 102.3 s | | r7 | 181 | 140 | 111 | 88 | 72 | 83.6 s | | r8 | 186* | 155* | 121 | 94 | 77 | 77.6 s | | r9 | 233* | 151* | 120 | 93 | 76 | 77.8 s | * For r8 and r9, the first two columns come from separate, shorter runs generating 2,032 tokens. The other columns come from the full-context run. r9 improves short-context speed, while the complete long-context run is roughly tied with r8. What the model actually says These examples come from the final r9 image. Arithmetic, with the steps Read the arithmetic transcript USER: What is 37 × 48? Explain the steps briefly. MODEL: <think> We need to compute 37 × 48. The user asks to explain steps briefly. So I'll do multiplication: 37 × 48 = 37 × (50 - 2) = 37×50 - 37×2 = 1850 - 74 = 1776. Or directly: 37×40=1480, 37×8=296, sum=1776. I'll present a brief explanation. </think> To multiply 37 by 48, you can break it down: - 37 × 48 = 37 × (50 – 2) = (37 × 50) – (37 × 2) = 1850 – 74 = 1776. Alternatively, 37 × 40 = 1480 and 37 × 8 = 296, so 1480 + 296 = 1776. The final answer is **1776**. A little Python System prompt: “You are a helpful assistant. Think briefly before you answer, then reply clearly and concisely.” Read the Python transcript USER: Write a Python function is_palindrome(s) that ignores case, spaces and punctuation. MODEL: <think> We need to write a Python function is_palindrome(s) that ignores case, spaces, and punctuation. So we need to filter out non-alphanumeric characters, convert to lowercase, then check if the resulting string is equal to its reverse. Provide the code. </think> ```python def is_palindrome(s: str) -> bool: """ Returns True if the string s is a palindrome, ignoring case, spaces, and punctuation. """ # Filter to keep only alphanumeric characters and convert to lowercase filtered = ''.join(ch.lower() for ch in s if ch.isalnum()) # Compare with its reverse return filtered == filtered[::-1] ``` Where this puts us This was a fun project. candidates.title: The best apps to make new friends right now
candidates.summary: In recent years, people have been increasingly looking for new ways to form platonic connections, as loneliness and social isolation have become more prevalent. In 2023, the U.S. Surgeon General went so far as to label this issue a public health crisis. Remote workers, who miss the everyday interact
candidates.full: In recent years, people have been increasingly looking for new ways to form platonic connections, as loneliness and social isolation have become more prevalent. In 2023, the U.S. Surgeon General went so far as to label this issue a public health crisis. Remote workers, who miss the everyday interactions found in an office, and younger individuals eager to create their adult social circles based on shared interests and hobbies, are among those seeking meaningful friendships. Thanks to online dating apps, the stigma associated with finding connections online has largely faded away. This has welcomed a new wave of apps focused on fostering friendships and building local communities. According to estimates from Appfigures, over a dozen local-focused friendship apps have collectively generated approximately $16 million in consumer spending in the U.S. so far this year. Some notable examples include Timeleft, Meet5, and Bumble’s BFF. Additionally, these apps have garnered approximately 4.3 million downloads thus far in 2025. The apps aim to provide a less awkward solution than, for instance, approaching a stranger at the gym or local café and trying to strike up a conversation. These platforms clearly indicate that everyone using the app is looking for the same thing — friendship, not romance — making it much less intimidating to initiate conversations. From major players like Meetup to newer ones like 222, there are plenty of apps that cater to the growing demand for meaningful friendships. We’ve compiled a list of them for you to try out. 222 The app 222 is an iOS-only social events platform that facilitates in-person meetups by pairing a group of strangers based on their personality test results. The app sends invitations to nearby public social events, such as wine bars and comedy clubs. There is then a vetting process, and selected participants are notified on the day of the event. A bonus for those who feel socially anxious: You’re allowed to bring a plus-one. The service charges a $22.22 curation fee or a monthly subscription for the same price. Bumble BFF Dating giant Bumble is among the more established players to enter the friendship space, launching its friend-finding feature in 2016, which then spun out into a stand-alone app in 2023. The friend-making app has recently undergone a significant redesign, with an increased emphasis on facilitating group meetups, catering to users’ desires to grow their social circles. BFF is available for free download on iOS and Android devices. Clyx Clyx is another emerging app in the group-based social networking landscape, with a strong focus on discovering local events. The social platform helps users find community events by integrating data from platforms like Ticketmaster and TikTok. Additionally, Clyx allows users to upload their contact lists, helping them see which events their friends plan to attend. The app also includes a feature that recommends other users to connect with at these events. As of now, Clyx operates exclusively in two cities: Miami and London. However, it has plans to expand to additional areas in the near future, with New York City and São Paulo at the top of the list. The app is available on the App Store and Google Play Store. Crowdier Crowdier is a new group social app that lets friend groups connect with others. Users can create a group of 2-5 friends and browse other groups to arrange hangouts in person. To initiate a match, users can “Wave” at groups they like, and if those groups wave back, they can plan in a shared chat. A match requires the majority of both groups to agree. For example, 2 people in a 4-person group needs to say yes. The app is available for free on iOS and Android devices. Les Amís Les Amís is a friendship app tailored for women, transgender, and LGBTQ+ individuals that leverages AI to match users based on similar interests and encourages participation in local events, such as pottery classes, book clubs, and wine tastings. Matches are made every Monday, allowing users to chat and plan meetups later in the week. Available on iOS and Android, Les Amís serves cities across Europe, including Amsterdam, Barcelona, Berlin, Madrid, Paris, and Stockholm. In the U.S., the app is available in Austin and New York, with plans to expand to Boston, Miami, and Los Angeles. The app uses a paid membership model that varies by city, with fees of $70 in New York and €55 in Amsterdam. Meetup The local event-discovery platform has been around since 2002, helping millions of users connect with others who share similar interests. Users can RSVP to events; join groups that cater to a variety of hobbies, professions, or social causes; and create their own groups and events. They can also chat with group members and post updates and photos from gatherings. Meet5 This European community-building app recently launched in the U.S., targeting users over 40 who want to meet new people in their area and participate in group activities such as picnics, concerts, and hiking. Notably, in a short time, there have been around 777,000 U.S. downloads so far across the App Store and Google Play Store, according to Appfigures estimates. Pie Pie is another one of the newer social apps on the market. It features an AI-driven quiz designed to predict which users are most likely to be compatible with each other. Each person who RSVPs to a Pie event takes a brief personality assessment, and the algorithm organizes attendees into groups of six, who are then added to a group chat within the Pie app, allowing them to interact with each other before the event. Currently, the app is only available in Austin, Chicago, and San Francisco. Users can download Pie from the App Store and Google Play Store. Timeleft Timeleft is a relatively new platform that helps you organize weekly dinner dates with groups of strangers. The app uses a special algorithm to match you with others, taking into account your age, gender, and personality. Users are matched with four other people, but they only learn minor details about them the night before, including their occupations and zodiac signs. Dinners take place at a selected restaurant on Wednesday evenings at 7:00 p.m. To help everyone break the ice, the app offers a game with conversation starters. After dinner, there is an after-party at a local bar. Users can book dinners online or through the app. In terms of pricing, it varies depending on the country and restaurant. Users pay for a ticket up front and are responsible for covering their own dinner and drinks. Washed Up Washed Up is a social event discovery app that launched in early 2026, designed for people in the Los Angeles area who want an easier way to find things to do and meet new people. The app helps users discover local events, such as concerts, trivia nights, and comedy shows, while also giving them a built-in way to connect with others who plan to attend. Instead of going to events alone, users can create or join “plans,” which are small group meetups tied to specific events. Users can browse these plans and request to join, chat with the group, and add new friends, making it easier to show up to events with people rather than by themselves. It’s available to download on the App Store. Wyzr Friends Wyzr Friends is an activity-based friendship app designed for adults 40 and older, catering to empty nesters, those who are divorced, and other users seeking to connect with like-minded individuals. Users can thumbs up or down potential friends and arrange in-person activities based on shared interests, such as going to the movies or hiking. It’s available on iOS and Android devices in the U.S., Canada, Australia, Ireland, the Philippines, Singapore, and Mexico. Mmotion Mmotion is a newly launched friendship app that blends location tracking with social discovery to help users connect with people nearby and explore new bars and restaurants in their area. Upon joining, users can participate in interest-based groups — such as hiking, basketball, or art — view a map of active users, and send messages to those nearby. The app also highlights new places on the map, making it easy to find a restaurant or venue to try. Mmotion is currently only available to users in New York City on iOS and Android devices. Users must first submit an application to be considered. Synchrony Launched in March 2026, Synchrony is a new social app tailored for neurodivergent adults. Founded by a mother of a son on the autism spectrum, it aims to create a supportive community through features like interest-based matching and two-step identity verification. This ensures that users engage safely, as both a user and a trusted person must verify personal details and a photo ID during registration. A standout feature is Jesse, an optional AI communication tool that assists users in navigating conversations. The AI provides editable prompts to help express thoughts, clarifies conversations, and offers boundary-setting suggestions. While the incorporation of AI may raise concerns, there are guardrails built into Jesse, such as avoiding medical advice. Users must pay a monthly subscription of $44.99 after a 30-day free trial. It’s available on iOS and Android devices. This story was updated after publication.

candidates.title: Researchers Hack Volkswagen Cars via Bluetooth to Spy on Conversations and Track GPS Locations
candidates.summary: Bluetooth flaws in Volkswagen cars could expose private conversations, reveal GPS locations, and allow unauthorized control of cabin features. The findings highlight a lengthy patch rollout, with some vehicles remaining exposed roughly 16 months after the vulnerabilities became public. Hungarian fir
candidates.full: Bluetooth flaws in Volkswagen cars could expose private conversations, reveal GPS locations, and allow unauthorized control of cabin features. The findings highlight a lengthy patch rollout, with some vehicles remaining exposed roughly 16 months after the vulnerabilities became public. Hungarian firm PCA Cyber Security demonstrated the attack against a Volkswagen ID.4 in Budapest, according to heise’s report. Researchers reportedly accessed the hands-free microphone, monitored location data, and operated the heater, windshield wipers, and sunroof using a laptop outside the vehicle. The attack uses PerfektBlue, a chain of vulnerabilities in OpenSynergy’s BlueSDK Bluetooth software. This component handles wireless connections in vehicle infotainment systems. PCA’s security advisory explains how the flaws can be combined to run attacker-controlled code on affected systems. For the demonstrated Volkswagen attack, the driver must first approve a Bluetooth pairing request. Once connected, the attacker can exploit the vulnerable software and gain control over functions available through the infotainment system. That requirement is important. The demonstration does not show that an attacker can silently compromise every nearby Volkswagen without interaction. Rejecting an unfamiliar pairing request blocks the connection this attack needs. Cyber Security News previously covered the underlying weaknesses in its report on the PerfektBlue Bluetooth vulnerabilities, which affected software used across multiple vehicle brands. Researchers estimate that several hundred thousand Volkswagen vehicles could be affected. However, that figure is not a confirmed count of compromised cars, and the reported demonstration does not establish widespread criminal exploitation. Volkswagen told heise that older infotainment software required additional changes and security checks, which delayed repairs. The company said it had addressed the issue more quickly in newer software branches. For vehicles running software older than version 4.0, Volkswagen says version 3.9.1 fixes the vulnerability. Eligible owners can install that update over cellular or Wi-Fi while their vehicle is parked. Other affected software versions require a workshop visit. Volkswagen says vehicles running version 5.6 or later are not affected. Owners should confirm the correct update route with Volkswagen rather than assume every car receives the same fix. Volkswagen says the flaws do not provide access to steering, braking, or acceleration. The demonstrated access instead concerns infotainment and connected cabin functions. Nevertheless, microphone access could expose sensitive conversations, while GPS tracking could reveal journeys and regular destinations. Those privacy risks remain significant even when driving controls are outside the attacker’s reach. Earlier research also identified separate weaknesses affecting vehicle data and infotainment systems, as detailed in Cyber Security News’ coverage of Skoda and Volkswagen security flaws. Those findings should not be treated as the same vulnerability chain. Volkswagen advises owners never to accept unknown Bluetooth pairing requests or connect unfamiliar USB devices. Drivers should check their installed software version, follow official update instructions, and contact a dealer when patch availability is unclear. Volkswagen has not announced a recall for this issue, according to heise’s report. candidates.full: 💬 Скандальная ситуация на наших глазах сейчас происходит вокруг участия российских спортсменов в мировых первенствах, в частности, в чемпионатах мира по хоккею. Во-первых, мы хотели бы ещё раз поприветствовать справедливое решение Международного спортивного арбитражного суда, в соответствии с которым сборная России по хоккею восстановила право участвовать в международных турнирах. Это решение стало предвестником возвращения в мировой спорт подлинно спортивного духа. <...> Но с подобным развитием событий согласны далеко не все. На передовой русофобии оказался премьер-министр Канады Марк Карни. <...> Он заявил, что принял решение — в нарушение Олимпийской хартии и обязательств, данных канадской хоккейной федерацией при подаче заявки на проведение молодёжного чемпионата мира по хоккею, — использовать все имеющиеся в его распоряжении возможности, вплоть до подключения миграционной службы, для того чтобы не допустить участия российских хоккеистов в мировом первенстве. <...> И это Канада, которой бы, честно говоря, отойти бы в угол и там каяться за всё то, что она натворила после Второй мировой, приютив у себя такое количество нацистов. Ну а с другой стороны, может, «руки помнят» . <...> Давайте вспомним такую позорнейшую историю, как существовавшие с 1883 по 1996 год — то есть больше 100 лет (!) — интернаты для детей индейцев. Через так называемую машину оккультуривания и приобщения, как они говорили, к цивилизации прошли более 150 тысяч детей. <...> Но ожидать какой-то моральной рефлексии от таких людей, как Марк Карни, я думаю, бессмысленно. <...> Он с гордостью заявляет, что, победив мальчишек-хоккеистов, он озаботился архитектурой безопасности в Европе в целом. Россия, в отличие от Канады, как сказал Карни, не должна участвовать в вопросах формирования архитектуры безопасности в Европе <...> Я хотела бы задать вопрос: Карни знает географию так же, как Бербок или Трасс, или ещё хуже? Где Канада, а где Европа? Подарите ему карту географическую. *** Мы уже говорили на одном из брифингов о дискриминационном решении Финляндии запретить въезд российским спортсменам. На этой неделе власти Норвегии также решили примкнуть к коалиции нежелающих состязаться на равных условиях и объявили о запрете въезда для российских и белорусских спортсменов, даже выступающих в нейтральном статусе. <...> Они заявили, что наши спортсмены не имеют равных прав с остальными, потому что они русские. Я не уверена, что тут что-то можно сказать или что-то как-то обозначить как лучше или хуже. Тут всё мерзко и отвратительно. *** Но правда, есть и те, которые, не могу сказать, стали звёздами, но точно звезданулись. Это, безусловно, министр иностранных дел Чехии Петр Маценко. Он, видимо, так испугался перспективы участия российских хоккеисток в юниорском чемпионате мира 2027 года в Остраве, что назвал россиянок (напомню, речь идёт о юниорском турнире) «мужеподобными девушками» 🤦‍♀️ Чешская общественность отреагировала на подобные оскорбительные выпады крайне негативно. Подобная «обратная связь» так впечатлила незадачливого политика, что он незамедлительно решил пробить очередной уровень европейской дипломатии, поспешив объясниться, что «мужеподобными» назвал исключительно российских хоккеисток, а не чешских. То есть свою вот такую какую-то предвзятость в отношении к людям по гендерному принципу он решил исправить просто откровенным расизмом и неонацизмом. <...> *** Мы усматриваем попытку коллективного Запада препятствовать возвращению одной из лучших мировых команд на международные турниры. Мы усматриваем в этом вашу откровенную банальную трусость. Вы боитесь проиграть. Вы боитесь в том числе и киевского режима, который вот так вами распоряжается. <...> Потому что мы опираемся на истинные ценности, мы не отказались от героев нашего с вами общего прошлого, потому что мы встали за них, когда они уже не могут отстоять себя. Когда мы исповедуем антифашизм по-настоящему, а не только раз в году. *** 🏒 Как не вспомнить строки о том, что «трус не играет в хоккей». Потому что хоккей без российских спортсменов — ну какой это мировой хоккей?

candidates.title: Prisons get OK to jam contraband phones
candidates.summary: The Federal Communications Commission yesterday voted to let state and local prisons use jamming technology to block contraband cellphones, despite warnings that jammers will also block lawful phone calls outside the prisons. Wireless industry lobby group CTIA said a recent test it conducted with th
candidates.full: The Federal Communications Commission yesterday voted to let state and local prisons use jamming technology to block contraband cellphones, despite warnings that jammers will also block lawful phone calls outside the prisons. Wireless industry lobby group CTIA said a recent test it conducted with the Virginia Tech Applied Research Corporation and South Carolina Department of Corrections confirmed concerns that the jammers would block legitimate communications, including 911 calls. CTIA told the FCC in an October 1 filing: The pilot test was limited in the number of micro-jammers deployed, the spectrum bands they were authorized to jam, and the power levels at which they were permitted to operate. Even with these constraints, the micro-jamming system blocked 911 calls, interfered with public safety and other communications, and caused interference that impacted wireless network infrastructure up to two and a half miles away. At the same time, the pilot results show substantial gaps in jamming the targeted “contraband” devices, with testing scenarios in outdoor inmate recreation areas showing failure rates—meaning “contraband” device call completion—in one-half to two-thirds of call attempts. CTIA said the pilot test shows “that current jamming technology seems to be both over and underinclusive at once—it risks blocking lawful communications even as it fails to block a significant portion of the targeted contraband device communications.” The FCC approved the jamming order at its meeting yesterday. “Today, we are finally authorizing state and local prisons and jails to use targeted jamming against contraband cell phones for the first time,” FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said. “The technology has advanced to the point where it can be focused with geographic precision. No facility will be required to do it.” The Communications Act prohibits willful or malicious interference with licensed or authorized radio communications, and the FCC has previously interpreted this to prohibit non-federal entities from using jamming technology on contraband devices at prisons. Yesterday’s vote provides an exception for state and local correctional facilities. The FCC says its jammer prohibitions do not apply to federal agencies because the federal government’s use of spectrum is not regulated by the agency.

Congressman Jim Himes, who will head the House Intelligence Committee in January, demanded that it be determined who ordered the communications used by the Armed Forces of Ukraine to be slowed. He sent a classified letter to US Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton and also requested an explanation from Musk himself. "Our committee cannot authorize funds to develop government systems that the government will not fully control," Himes’s letter says. ️Earlier, Musk accused Zelensky of lying following his statements about the satellite communications restrictions. The entrepreneur claimed that Starlink is not intended for offensive operations, while the Starshield military system is under the control of the US government. At the same time, The Wall Street Journal wrote that it was Musk who ordered communications for Ukraine to be slowed. Our channel: Node of Time EN

candidates.title: No fanfare for Albanese after whirlwind trip abroad
candidates.summary: Returning home from 11 days of being feted on the world stage, the economic reality will hit Anthony Albanese with a thud. The prime minister was hailed by Chinese President Xi Jinping for helping achieve a "full turnaround" in relations between the two nations in Shenzhen on Friday, held after the
candidates.full: Returning home from 11 days of being feted on the world stage, the economic reality will hit Anthony Albanese with a thud. The prime minister was hailed by Chinese President Xi Jinping for helping achieve a "full turnaround" in relations between the two nations in Shenzhen on Friday, held after the conclusion of the APEC summit. It was the final leg of a three-nation tour, taking in the COP climate conference in Turkey and the ASEAN summit in the Philippines. With 21 of the world's top nations gathered at the APEC summit, it gave Mr Albanese an opportunity to spruik Australia's agenda for AI standards, open trade and deescalation of wars in Ukraine and the Middle East. But his contributions were overshadowed by a historic trilateral meeting between the leaders of China, Russia and the US held on its sidelines. The talks, held a day before Mr Albanese met with Mr Xi, drew comparisons to the 1945 Yalta conference, where the US, Britain and the Soviet Union divided up the ruins of Europe between themselves. The fear was that the meeting could herald a return to major powers carving the globe up into spheres of influence, leaving middle powers like Australia, Japan and Ukraine with little autonomy. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy feared his country's future being decided without him in the room. But Nick Bisley, an international relations expert at La Trobe University, said while the meeting was long on symbolism, it was short on substance. "Trump will be gone in two years and while the domestic focus is likely to remain, the kind of personalised leadership he has pursued, that allowed this kind of meeting, is unlikely to persist," he told AAP. In the end, Ukraine barely rated a mention in the meeting. Rather than heralding a shift away from multilateralism, the fact the meeting occurred on the sidelines of a multilateral meeting showed they remain relevant, Professor Bisley said. Indeed, Mr Trump's attendance at the Quad leaders' meeting - with Mr Albanese, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and India's Narendra Modi on the sidelines of ASEAN in Manila - revitalised the institution, which analysts argued had shrunk in stature during Mr Trump's second term. The fact that the four nations agreed to hold military exercises together for the first time, with Australia contributing P-8 and P-C3 patrol aircraft, was an indication that the US still devotes at least some of its focus to the Asia-Pacific. "Australia's real focus is on East Asia, and the agreements at ASEAN and the revitalisation of the Quad are probably the most important achievements," Prof Bisley said. "More generally, Australia has a vital interest in ensuring the multilateral structures function and deliver, and in contributing to this, Australia had advanced its interests." Whether this is enough to justify his 11-day trip to voters back home is another matter. Much of the focus was taken up by criticism about spending at the COP climate conference in Turkey, a ribald conversation with Climate Change Minister Chris Bowen caught on hot-mic, and his appearance in a staged group photo with Russia's president. But arguably the most critical development during the trip happened at home, when the Australian Bureau of Statistics revealed unemployment jumped to a five-year high of 4.9 per cent in October. Mr Albanese will get little reward from voters for taking China-Australia relations to new heights, but if the economy slides into a recession, he will shoulder all of the blame. Australian Associated Press

candidates.full: Менше кінських сил, але швидше на треку. Ferrari представила чисто бензиновий суперкар 296 Challenge Stradale Ferrari 296 Challenge Stradale (Фото: Ferrari) Ferrari прибрала гібридну частину зі свого шестициліндрового суперкара, втратила понад півтори сотні кінських сил, але отримала помітно швидшу машину на треку. Італійська марка представила дорожню модель 296 Challenge Stradale, яка переносить гоночні напрацювання без електричної надбудови на звичайні вулиці. Про це пише Auto Blog. Раніше негібридні версії із трилітровим турбованим V6 компанія випускала лише для треку, наприклад 296 GT3 та 296 Challenge. Тепер нова 296 Challenge Stradale відкриває цей формат для доріг загального користування і націлена на покупців, які обирають між подібними трековими моделями на кшталт Porsche 911 GT3 RS. Новинка розвиває 661 кінську силу, проте має суху масу 1330 кілограмів, що приблизно на 140 кілограмів менше за базовий гібридний 296 GTB потужністю 819 кінських сил. Завдяки розширеному передньому сплітеру, закритому днищу, генераторам вихорів і фіксованому задньому антикрилу суперкар створює 617 кілограмів притискної сили на швидкості 250 кілометрів на годину. У підсумку фірмову трасу у Фйорано модель проходить за 1 хвилину 18,5 секунди, приблизно на 2,5 секунди швидше за 296 GTB. Водночас Ferrari представила суто трековий варіант 296 Challenge Evo потужністю 690 кінських сил. Він отримав на 12 відсотків більше притискної сили, покращені гальма та оновлену електроніку, що дає змогу проходити коло на трасі Муджелло на 0,8 секунди швидше за попередника. За даними Car and Driver, в Італії 296 Challenge Stradale коштуватиме від 291 тисячі євро, а поставки до США розпочнуться наприкінці 2027 року. Відмова від гібрида вписується в оновлену стратегію Ferrari до 2030 року. Якщо раніше бренд планував 40 відсотків електромобілів і лише 20 відсотків чисто бензинових авто, то тепер орієнтується на 40 відсотків бензинових моделей, 40 відсотків гібридів і 20 відсотків електрокарів.

candidates.full: «Моральна катастрофа». Лише 6% переконані, що РФ має відповідати за жертви та руйнування в Україні — опитування Зокрема, як з’ясували соціологи Левада-центру, дві третини росіян (65%) вважають, що «відповідальність за наслідки війни повинні нести США та НАТО» (Фото: REUTERS/Marina Lystseva) Лише 6% жителів країни-агресора РФ вважають, що Росія повинна відповідати за ті жертви й руйнування, які спричинили російські окупанти в Україні. Про це 20 повідомляє видання The Moscow Times з посиланням на дослідження соціологів із «Левада-центру». Зокрема, саме такі дані на конференції Країна і світ: російські реалії 2026 року навів керівник відділу соціокультурних досліджень установи Олексій Левінсон. Зокрема, як з’ясували соціологи Левада-центру, дві третини росіян (65%) вважають, що «відповідальність за наслідки війни повинні нести США та НАТО». При цьому більшість респондентів не вважають відповідальними за те, що відбувається, людей, схожих на них самих. Лише 11% відповіли, що відчувають таку відповідальність, 57% заперечили її, а ще 25% заявили, що певною мірою її відчувають, повідомили в Левада-центрі. «Соціолог Лев Гудков називає це моральною катастрофою», — пише The Moscow Times. Більше того, 85−88% молодих росіян підтримали б припинення війни проти України, але лише за умови, що Кремлю не доведеться повертати тимчасово захоплені українські території, підсумували соціологи. 24 грудня 2025 року Левада-центр опублікував результати свого чергового опитування мешканців РФ. Тоді частка росіян, які вважають за необхідне продовжувати війну проти України, знизилася до 25% (найнижчий показник за весь час повномасштабної війни). За даними цього опитування, рівень підтримки дій окупаційних військ в Україні серед росіян залишався відносно високим — 73%, але в останні місяці поступово знижувався. Водночас 18% росіян не підтримують дії окупаційної армії РФ. Опитування також показало, що 66% опитаних виступають за перехід до мирних переговорів, підсумували в «Левада-центрі».

candidates.full: 🤝 Українські дрони middle strike та deep strike вироблятимуть у Великій Британії для потреб Сил оборони. Міністр оборони України Євгеній Хмара та Міністр оборони Великої Британії Вес Стрітінг підписали відповідні проєктні домовленості щодо спільного виробництва. Українські безпілотники, які вже довели свою ефективність, вироблятимуть за фінансування Великої Британії. Продукція спільних виробництв спрямовуватиметься на потреби українських воїнів. «Запускаємо проєкти, які посилюють спроможності обох наших країн та пришвидшують розвиток наших ОПК. Україна має дієві оборонні рішення та неоціненний досвід боротьби з ворогом. Поєднуємо їх із виробничими можливостями Великої Британії, щоб швидше масштабувати перевірені засоби для наших Сил оборони. Для нас важлива стійкість нашого партнерства, його якість і здатність давати результат у довгостроковій перспективі» , — наголосив Євгеній Хмара. Велика Британія стала однією з перших країн, які оперативно передали Україні ракети LMM із власних складів в обмін на майбутні поставки. Такі засоби критично важливі для протидії реактивним «шахедам». Під час зустрічі Міністр подякував Великій Британії за лідерство у підтримці України та пакет допомоги для протиповітряної оборони, оголошений під час «Рамштайну». Сторони сфокусувалися на подальших кроках для зміцнення української ППО — зокрема, прискоренні нових поставок ракет LMM із наявних запасів. Також зосередилися на посиленні далекобійних спроможностей України та модернізації ракет українського виробництва.

candidates.title: ¿Cuánto viviremos los humanos gracias a la IA?: la respuesta de un filósofo sorprende
candidates.summary: Los seres humanos podrían vivir más de un milenio si la inteligencia artificial logra avances revolucionarios en biomedicina e investigación antienvejecimiento que extiendan radicalmente la esperanza de vida, según el filósofo sueco y exprofesor de Oxford Nick Bostrom, informó Business Insider el 20
candidates.full: Los seres humanos podrían vivir más de un milenio si la inteligencia artificial logra avances revolucionarios en biomedicina e investigación antienvejecimiento que extiendan radicalmente la esperanza de vida, según el filósofo sueco y exprofesor de Oxford Nick Bostrom, informó Business Insider el 20 noviembre. "Si piensas en cuál sería nuestra esperanza de vida si no estuviéramos envejeciendo, es algo del orden de, ya sabes, 1.200, tal vez 1.400 años, más o menos", sostiene Bostrom. "Y eso tal vez sea un límite inferior bastante conservador, porque en esta situación también podrías tener otras formas de reducir otros riesgos de mortalidad, como accidentes y demás", añade. Bostrom, que estudia la mejora humana y las tecnologías emergentes, fundó en Oxford el Instituto del Futuro de la Humanidad en 2005 como grupo de investigación multidisciplinario, que finalmente cerró en 2024. Sus comentarios se producen mientras la seguridad de la IA se ha convertido en un tema cada vez más debatido, siendo cada vez más los investigadores que piden que se ralentice su desarrollo para abordar problemas de alineación y establecer las salvaguardas adecuadas. El filósofo señala que el equilibrio entre desarrollar la IA rápidamente y garantizar su seguridad es complicado. "Por un lado, podrías pensar que si tomáramos un tiempo extra con esta transición de IA, tal vez podríamos construir IA de manera más segura", indica. "Entonces podrías pensar que si pasamos más tiempo haciendo investigación sobre alineación de IA, el riesgo existencial de desarrollar IA disminuye a cierta tasa. Y por otro lado, cada año que lo retrasamos, tenemos millones y millones de personas muriendo", concluye Bostrom.

candidates.full: #СатирКаГоворит Татьяна Ким перестала быть гендиректором ООО «Вайлдберриз» . Основательницу маркетплейса сменил топ-менеджер Алексей Куликов, ранее занимавший руководящие должности в компании. Изменения отражены в ЕГРЮЛ – на них также обратили внимание каналы, следящие за работой маркетплейсов. Кадровая перестановка совпала с изменениями в структуре объединенного бизнеса Wildberries и Russ. Доля ООО «Вайлдберриз» в компании РВБ сократилась с 65% до 45%, а доля ООО «Стинн» – с 35% до 25%. Новыми участниками стали два закрытых паевых фонда: «Томь» получил 17,5%, «Гало» – 12,5%. Таким образом, фондам теперь принадлежит 30% объединённой компании . Изменения произошли вскоре после того, как Евросоюз ввел санкци против Ким. Некоторые каналы предполагают , что перестановки связаны именно с ограничениями. Совпадение по времени заметное, однако официально такую причину не подтвердили . Ранее в RWB заявляли, что санкции не повлияют на работу компании и её сервисов. При этом уход с поста директора отдельного юрлица не означает ухода Ким из бизнеса . В RWB сообщили, что она продолжит заниматься стратегическим развитием группы, а смена руководителя не затронет операционную деятельность маркетплейса. Компания продолжает развивать экосистему: в том числе, как пишут каналы, готовит собственный сервис для общения. Для покупателей и продавцов главный вопрос – отразятся ли перестановки на работе площадки. Компания уверяет, что нет . Но изменение состава участников и смена директора все же показывают: структура одного из крупнейших российских маркетплейсов продолжает меняться. А насколько вместе с ней меняется реальное распределение влияния , пока остается открытым вопросом. Подписывайтесь на канал 👈

candidates.title: Elon Musk’s most unbelievable claim yet
candidates.summary: President Donald Trump may be starting to feel lonely without his tech buddies around. candidates.full: President Donald Trump may be starting to feel lonely without his tech buddies around. First Jensen Huang had his spectacular fall from Nvidia, and in an even crueler cut, Elon Musk is acting like he and Trump never had the tempestuous bromance we all suffered through for the last two years. “I’m not MAGA,” Musk said, calling in to The New York Times’ DealBook Summit on Wednesday. “I’m not sure what MAGA means, but if that means sort of blind adherence to a set of policies by the Republican Party, then I certainly don’t have that.” What about all those times he appeared in MAGA hats, or joined Trump in 2024 at campaign rallies, or proclaimed, “I’m not just MAGA, I’m dark MAGA!” (whatever that means), or joined the Trump administration to rampage through the federal government with catastrophic results? Are we supposed to forget all that? Perhaps when you own your own social media platform, make insane predictions people somehow take seriously despite the fact that they seem to never come true and became a trillionaire by pumping wildly inflated stock prices, you think the rubes will buy anything you tell them. But here’s the irony: It’s true there is a large group of Americans who have been quite willing to believe even the most bizarre and obviously false rewriting of history. But they’re precisely the ones from whom Musk is now trying to distance himself. To be a true devotee of Trump, after all, requires the ability to adopt new deranged and provably false beliefs at a moment’s notice, should Trump tell you to do so. The 2020 election? Stolen. The 2024 election that Trump won by 1.5 percentage points? A huge landslide. The violent Jan. 6 insurrection? A “day of love.” The Covid-19 pandemic that killed over 1.2 million Americans? The real tragedy was the measures taken to prevent the spread of the virus. Any and every problem the Trump administration has failed to solve? Joe Biden’s fault. But even the most gullible Trump fan won’t be inclined to believe that Musk was never MAGA in the first place. And the rest of us are even less than inclined to welcome him back to the population of the sane. Trump, uncharacteristically, appeared to take Musk’s comments with surprising equanimity. “There are lots of definitions out there,” Trump told NBC News. “MAGA, to me, means something very specific, and when people veer from it, they don’t do very well.” It’s possible to read that as a warning, or just as a kind of self-soothing; Trump reassuring himself that he and his movement are still popular. Because after the midterm elections, it’s pretty obvious that sticking too close to MAGA, not veering from it, is what causes one to not “do very well.” Musk found that out the hard way, having just spent nearly half a billion dollars in support of GOP candidates in a midterm cycle that Republicans overwhelmingly lost. He told the Times, “I feel pretty foolish about having spent so much money and not seeing much for it.” But don’t expect Democrats to welcome him back with open arms. While he had much to gain from his alliance with Trump — a steady supply of government contracts and the quashing of investigations into his companies, among other things — the Trump-Musk bond was built on more than self-interest. Musk was and remains MAGA in the deepest sense. It’s true that the foundation of MAGA is its cult-like devotion to Trump himself. But the movement does have a discernible worldview, at least on a few issues. Primary among them is immigration, where the movement is intensely nativist, opposed to immigration and often nakedly racist. So are the many statements of Musk. Even if one wants to be generous to him about that salute, he posts relentlessly on X about race, railing against non-white immigration to America and Europe and toying with eugenicist ideas. He uses his platform to promote far-right parties around the globe. These are not the actions of a clear-eyed capitalist; if anything, they do significant harm to his businesses. We can therefore only surmise that they represent Musk’s sincere beliefs. No one is going to believe Musk if he tries to reinvent himself as nonpolitical in response to the new realities of power in Washington. Democrats certainly don’t; they are preparing multiple investigations into his billions of dollars in federal contracts, the wreckage he caused with the Department of Government Efficiency and whether he throttled the Starlink internet service on which the Ukrainian military relies. Those are all legitimate lines of inquiry, and if there’s a bit of revenge mixed in? Musk can only blame himself. Meanwhile, Trump isn’t willing to let Musk go. “I helped Elon a lot in my first term,” he said this week, adding that “a lot of people don’t know that, you wouldn’t probably have Elon today” — if it weren’t for him, of course. Which isn’t quite true, but it’s a reminder of what the two men have in common: oversized egos, an ability to seize almost limitless attention in the social media age, ugly ideological beliefs and a faith that they can convince the masses of almost anything. They may not always get along, but they will forever be tied together. The post Elon Musk’s most unbelievable claim yet appeared first on MS NOW.

Αυτοί οι τύποι είναι πολύ ισχυροί (το CNN έδειξε παράλληλα μερικές φωτογραφίες του Μασκ και του Τραμπ ). Στις Ηνωμένες Πολιτείες δεν είναι μόνο τα χρήματα που τα αποφασίζουν όλα. Είμαι ευγνώμων προς την Space X και την κυβέρνηση των ΗΠΑ για ό,τι έχει γίνει. Αλλά αν αυτό δεν λειτουργεί, τότε δεν λειτουργεί», δήλωσε ο Ουκρανός πρόεδρος. candidates.summary: Зеленський розповів про переговори з Росією, роль Європи та нові гуманітарні місії на ТОТ Президент України Володимир Зеленський відповів на запитання журналістів щодо перспектив завершення війни в Україні, участі європейських партнерів у переговорах з Росією. Можливих зустрічей з лідерами США і Рос
candidates.full: Зеленський розповів про переговори з Росією, роль Європи та нові гуманітарні місії на ТОТ Президент України Володимир Зеленський відповів на запитання журналістів щодо перспектив завершення війни в Україні, участі європейських партнерів у переговорах з Росією. Можливих зустрічей з лідерами США і Росії та підготовку нових гуманітарних операцій для евакуації українців з тимчасово окупованих територій. Про це він повідомив, відповідаючи на запитання журналістів у вотсап-групі пресслужби Офісу президента. Зеленський прокоментував можливість проведення тристороннього саміту за участю України, США та Росії на полях G20. «Передусім наші радники з питань нацбезпеки будуть мати низку контактів: може, у відеоформаті, може, офлайн — подивимося. Для того, щоб підготувати адженду, тобто зміст для зустрічей і результат цієї зустрічі. Максимальний, середній, мінімальний — що ми маємо дати для деескалації, як наблизити всіх нас до закінчення цієї війни», — розповів президент. Він нагадав, що під час зустрічі в Берліні американська сторона висловлювала бажання провести відповідні переговори до Різдва. «Я їм сказав: “Ну до Різдва — безумовно. Можемо раніше — давайте робити раніше. Чим раніше можемо зробити якийсь результат — тим краще, збережемо людей”», — зазначив Зеленський. Водночас Україна поки не отримала офіційного запрошення від американської сторони взяти участь у саміті G20. «Я знаю, і мені це підтверджували вже багато лідерів, які запропонували американській стороні офіційно запросити Україну на G20, але ми поки що офіційного запрошення від Америки не отримували. Безумовно, якщо вони нас запросять — ми будемо брати участь», — повідомив президент. Він припустив, що на полях саміту може відбутися тристороння зустріч лідерів України, США та Росії. «Чи може бути така тристороння зустріч на полях G20 — я впевнений, що може бути. Ми чули, що деякі конгресмени не позитивно ставляться до того, що Путіна запросив Трамп. Але я думаю, що якщо Трамп запросить Україну — це трішечки інша історія. Тому що тристороння зустріч на полях G20 буде підтримана», — сказав глава держави. Також Зеленський заявив, що Україна підтримує залучення європейських країн до переговорного процесу. За його словами, участь Європи важлива не лише через спільні цінності, а й з практичних міркувань безпеки. «Ми ставимося позитивно. І це не тільки емоційно, не тільки про те, що ми поділяємо однакові цінності. Це дуже практично. Без Польщі не може бути перемовин, як і без кожної з країн Європи», — наголосив президент. Він пояснив, що представляти європейську позицію у переговорному процесі мають п’ять країн, які називають форматом Е5: Велика Британія, Німеччина, Франція, Італія та Польща. До них долучаться два представники Європейського Союзу — від Європейської комісії та Європейської ради, а також представник НАТО. «Вони всі будуть разом обговорювати адженду в тісному співробітництві з нами, в постійних тісних консультаціях з Україною — і потім цю вже загальну адженду Європи будуть представляти відповідні країни і представники інституцій, про які я вже сказав», — пояснив глава держави. Президент наголосив, що європейська участь у переговорах має принципове значення, оскільки Україна прагне стати частиною Європейського Союзу, а багато європейських держав є її безпосередніми партнерами та сусідами Росії. «Все це дуже важливо, бо війна в Україні, а значить війна в Європі. Тому Європа обов'язково повинна бути тут. США сьогодні підтримують такий формат – чотиристоронніх зустрічей. Від США ми отримали сигнали, що начебто Росія не проти. Подивимося», — сказав Зеленський. Окрім того, президент повідомив про підготовку нових гуманітарних місій на тимчасово окупованих територіях Херсонської та Запорізької областей. Зеленський подякував першій леді США за сприяння в розблокуванні евакуації людей з Олешків. За його словами, Україна вже опрацювала оновлений перелік населених пунктів, який передали омбудсману та американській стороні. «Ми проговорили з головкомом Драпатим і сьогодні ще раз підтвердили список. Я його привітав з днем народження. І ми з ним детально поговорили щодо цих гуманітарних місій, щодо кількості людей, яких ми можемо евакуювати, і які напрацювання в нас є», — розповів президент. За його словами, до переліку населених пунктів Херсонської області, де планують провести гуманітарні операції, увійшли: - Раденськ; - Костогризове; - Гола Пристань; - Стара Збур'ївка; - Нова Збур'ївка; - Гладківка; - Великі Копані; - Кардашинка; - Велика Кардашинка. У Запорізькій області йдеться про такі населені пункти: - Маячка; - Златопіль; - Дніпрорудне; - Кам'янське; - Верхня Криниця; - Василівка. «Цей список буде оновлюватися. Буде опрацьовуватися, як тільки ми будемо мати повну інформацію і цифри, скільки людей, в якому стані відбувається в тому чи іншому місті, містечку нашої держави на тимчасово окупованих територіях», — підсумував президент. Нагадаємо, що, відповідаючи на запитання журналістів у вотсап-групі пресслужби Офісу президента, Володимир Зеленський заявив, що членство України в НАТО залишається найбільш зрозумілою гарантією безпеки для держави. Також глава держави додав, що Володимиру Путіну не вдалося реалізувати задум щодо нового переділу світу за результатами тристороннього саміту за участю США, Китаю та Росії. Окрім того, Володимир Зеленський заявив, що рішення щодо нового посла України у США ухвалять після отримання фінального звіту міністра закордонних справ Андрія Сибіги щодо кадрових змін у дипломатичному корпусі.
